483: fn approx_eq(a: f32, b: f32) -> bool {
484:     (a - b).abs() <= 1e-3
485: }

487: #[allow(
488:     clippy::too_many_lines,
489:     reason = "one cohesive widget-construction pass; splitting it would scatter GTK setup order"
490: )]
491: fn clip_shape_css(shape: &ClipShape) -> ClipShapeCss {
492:     let commands = shape.commands();
493:     match commands {
494:         [
495:             PathCommand::MoveTo { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 },
496:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 1.0, y: 0.0 },
497:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 },
498:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 },
499:             PathCommand::Close,
500:         ] => ClipShapeCss::Rectangle,
501:         [
502:             PathCommand::Arc {
503:                 cx,
504:                 cy,
505:                 rx,
506:                 ry,
507:                 start,
508:                 sweep,
509:             },
510:         ] if approx_eq(*cx, 0.5)
511:             && approx_eq(*cy, 0.5)
512:             && approx_eq(*rx, 0.5)
513:             && approx_eq(*ry, 0.5)
514:             && approx_eq(*start, 0.0)
515:             && approx_eq(*sweep, std::f32::consts::TAU) =>
516:         {
517:             ClipShapeCss::Ellipse
518:         }
519:         [
520:             PathCommand::MoveTo { x: tl, y: 0.0 },
521:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: x2, y: 0.0 },
522:             PathCommand::Arc {
523:                 cx: _,
524:                 cy: tr,
525:                 rx: top_right_radius_x,
526:                 ry: top_right_radius_y,
527:                 start: _,
528:                 sweep: _,
529:             },
530:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 1.0, y: y4 },
531:             PathCommand::Arc {
532:                 cx: _,
533:                 cy: _,
534:                 rx: bottom_right_radius_x,
535:                 ry: bottom_right_radius_y,
536:                 start: _,
537:                 sweep: _,
538:             },
539:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: bl, y: 1.0 },
540:             PathCommand::Arc {
541:                 cx: _,
542:                 cy: _,
543:                 rx: bottom_left_radius_x,
544:                 ry: bottom_left_radius_y,
545:                 start: _,
546:                 sweep: _,
547:             },
548:             PathCommand::LineTo { x: 0.0, y: y8 },
549:             PathCommand::Arc {
550:                 cx: _,
551:                 cy: _,
552:                 rx: top_left_radius_x,
553:                 ry: top_left_radius_y,
554:                 start: _,
555:                 sweep: _,
556:             },
557:             PathCommand::Close,
558:         ] => {
559:             let top_left = (*tl + *top_left_radius_x + *top_left_radius_y + *y8) / 4.0;
560:             let top_right = ((1.0 - *x2) + *tr + *top_right_radius_x + *top_right_radius_y) / 4.0;
561:             let bottom_right =
562:                 ((1.0 - *y4) + *bottom_right_radius_x + *bottom_right_radius_y) / 3.0;
563:             let bottom_left = (*bl + *bottom_left_radius_x + *bottom_left_radius_y) / 3.0;
564:             ClipShapeCss::Rounded {
565:                 top_left,
566:                 top_right,
567:                 bottom_right,
568:                 bottom_left,
569:             }
570:         }
571:         [
572:             PathCommand::MoveTo { x: 0.5, y: 0.0 },
573:             PathCommand::Arc {
574:                 cx: 0.5,
575:                 cy: 0.5,
576:                 rx: 0.5,
577:                 ry: 0.5,
578:                 start: _,
579:                 sweep: _,
580:             },
581:             PathCommand::Arc {
582:                 cx: 0.5,
583:                 cy: 0.5,
584:                 rx: 0.5,
585:                 ry: 0.5,
586:                 start: _,
587:                 sweep: _,
588:             },
589:             PathCommand::Close,
590:         ] => ClipShapeCss::Ellipse,
591:         _ => panic!("unsupported ClipShape path for GTK backend"),
592:     }
593: }

595: fn drag_content_provider(data: &DragData) -> gdk4::ContentProvider {
596:     let text = data.as_str().to_owned();
597:     let text_provider = gdk4::ContentProvider::for_value(&text.to_value());
598:     match data {
599:         DragData::Text(_) => text_provider,
600:         DragData::Url(_) => {
601:             let uri_list = format!("{text}\r\n");
602:             let uri_provider = gdk4::ContentProvider::for_bytes(
603:                 "text/uri-list",
604:                 &glib::Bytes::from(uri_list.as_bytes()),
605:             );
606:             gdk4::ContentProvider::new_union(&[text_provider, uri_provider])
607:         }
608:         _ => panic!("unsupported DragData variant on GTK backend"),
609:     }
610: }

612: fn drag_data_from_text(text: String) -> DragData {
613:     if text.starts_with("http://") || text.starts_with("https://") || text.starts_with("file://") {
614:         DragData::url(text)
615:     } else {
616:         DragData::text(text)

620: fn drag_data_from_drop_value(value: &glib::Value) -> Option<DragData> {
621:     if let Ok(text) = value.get::<String>() {
622:         return Some(drag_data_from_text(text));
623:     }
624:     if let Ok(text) = value.get::<glib::GString>() {
625:         return Some(drag_data_from_text(text.to_string()));
626:     }
627:     None

630: fn call_boxed_action(action: &Rc<RefCell<BoxedAction<()>>>, env: &Environment) {
631:     if let Ok(mut handler) = action.try_borrow_mut() {
632:         (**handler)(env);
633:     }

636: #[allow(
637:     clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
638:     clippy::cast_precision_loss,
639:     clippy::cast_sign_loss,
640:     reason = "GTK widget geometry is integer pixels while WaterUI layout is f32"
641: )]
642: #[allow(
643:     clippy::too_many_lines,
644:     reason = "one cohesive widget-construction pass; splitting it would scatter GTK setup order"
645: )]
646: fn install_gesture_observer(
647:     widget: &Widget,
648:     gesture: waterui::gesture::Gesture,
649:     action: Rc<RefCell<BoxedAction<()>>>,
650:     env: Environment,
651: ) {
652:     use waterui::gesture::{
653:         DragEvent, Gesture, GesturePhase, GesturePoint, LongPressEvent, MagnificationEvent,
654:         RotationEvent, TapEvent,
655:     };
656: 
657:     match gesture {
658:         Gesture::Tap(tap) => {
659:             let click = gtk4::GestureClick::new();
660:             click.set_button(1);
661:             click.set_propagation_phase(gtk4::PropagationPhase::Capture);
662:             let required_count = tap.count;
663:             let env_for_handler = env;
664:             let action_for_handler = action.clone();
665:             click.connect_pressed(move |gesture, n_press, x, y| {
666:                 if n_press as u32 >= required_count {
667:                     let tap_event = TapEvent {
668:                         location: GesturePoint::new(x as f32, y as f32),
669:                         count: n_press as u32,
670:                     };
671:                     let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
672:                     local_env.insert(tap_event);
673:                     call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
674:                     gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
675:                 }
676:             });
677:             widget.add_controller(click);
678:         }
679:         Gesture::LongPress(long_press) => {
680:             let press = gtk4::GestureLongPress::new();
681:             press.set_delay_factor(f64::from(long_press.duration) / 500.0);
682:             press.set_propagation_phase(gtk4::PropagationPhase::Capture);
683:             let env_for_handler = env;
684:             let action_for_handler = action.clone();
685:             let duration = long_press.duration;
686:             press.connect_pressed(move |gesture, x, y| {
687:                 let event = LongPressEvent {
688:                     location: GesturePoint::new(x as f32, y as f32),
689:                     duration: duration as f32,
690:                 };
691:                 let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
692:                 local_env.insert(event);
693:                 call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
694:                 gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
695:             });
696:             widget.add_controller(press);
697:         }
698:         Gesture::Drag(drag) => {
699:             let drag_gesture = gtk4::GestureDrag::new();
700:             drag_gesture.set_propagation_phase(gtk4::PropagationPhase::Capture);
701:             let min_distance = drag.min_distance;
702:             let drag_started = Rc::new(RefCell::new(false));
703:             {
704:                 let env_for_handler = env.clone();
705:                 let action_for_handler = action.clone();
706:                 let drag_started = drag_started.clone();
707:                 drag_gesture.connect_drag_begin(move |gesture, x, y| {
708:                     *drag_started.borrow_mut() = false;
709:                     let event = DragEvent {
710:                         phase: GesturePhase::Started,
711:                         location: GesturePoint::new(x as f32, y as f32),
712:                         translation: GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
713:                         velocity: GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
714:                     };
715:                     let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
716:                     local_env.insert(event);
717:                     call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
718:                     gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
719:                 });
720:             }
721:             {
722:                 let env_for_handler = env.clone();
723:                 let action_for_handler = action.clone();
724:                 let drag_started = drag_started.clone();
725:                 drag_gesture.connect_drag_update(move |gesture, offset_x, offset_y| {
726:                     let distance = offset_x.hypot(offset_y) as f32;
727:                     if distance < min_distance && !*drag_started.borrow() {
728:                         return;
729:                     }
730:                     *drag_started.borrow_mut() = true;
731:                     let start = gesture.start_point().unwrap_or((0.0, 0.0));
732:                     let event = DragEvent {
733:                         phase: GesturePhase::Updated,
734:                         location: GesturePoint::new(
735:                             (start.0 + offset_x) as f32,
736:                             (start.1 + offset_y) as f32,
737:                         ),
738:                         translation: GesturePoint::new(offset_x as f32, offset_y as f32),
739:                         velocity: GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
740:                     };
741:                     let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
742:                     local_env.insert(event);
743:                     call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
744:                 });
745:             }
746:             {
747:                 let env_for_handler = env;
748:                 let action_for_handler = action.clone();
749:                 drag_gesture.connect_drag_end(move |gesture, offset_x, offset_y| {
750:                     if !*drag_started.borrow() {
751:                         return;
752:                     }
753:                     let start = gesture.start_point().unwrap_or((0.0, 0.0));
754:                     let event = DragEvent {
755:                         phase: GesturePhase::Ended,
756:                         location: GesturePoint::new(
757:                             (start.0 + offset_x) as f32,
758:                             (start.1 + offset_y) as f32,
759:                         ),
760:                         translation: GesturePoint::new(offset_x as f32, offset_y as f32),
761:                         velocity: GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
762:                     };
763:                     let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
764:                     local_env.insert(event);
765:                     call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
766:                 });
767:             }
768:             widget.add_controller(drag_gesture);
769:         }
770:         Gesture::Magnification(_) => {
771:             let zoom = gtk4::GestureZoom::new();
772:             let env_for_handler = env;
773:             let action_for_handler = action.clone();
774:             zoom.connect_scale_changed(move |gesture, scale| {
775:                 let center = gesture.bounding_box().map_or_else(
776:                     || GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
777:                     |bbox| GesturePoint::new(bbox.x() as f32, bbox.y() as f32),
778:                 );
779:                 let event = MagnificationEvent {
780:                     phase: GesturePhase::Updated,
781:                     center,
782:                     scale: scale as f32,
783:                     velocity: 0.0,
784:                 };
785:                 let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
786:                 local_env.insert(event);
787:                 call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
788:                 gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
789:             });
790:             widget.add_controller(zoom);
791:         }
792:         Gesture::Rotation(_) => {
793:             let rotate = gtk4::GestureRotate::new();
794:             let env_for_handler = env;
795:             let action_for_handler = action.clone();
796:             rotate.connect_angle_changed(move |gesture, angle, _delta| {
797:                 let center = gesture.bounding_box().map_or_else(
798:                     || GesturePoint::new(0.0, 0.0),
799:                     |bbox| GesturePoint::new(bbox.x() as f32, bbox.y() as f32),
800:                 );
801:                 let event = RotationEvent {
802:                     phase: GesturePhase::Updated,
803:                     center,
804:                     angle: angle as f32,
805:                     // GTK reports no angular velocity, matching the zoom gesture.
806:                     velocity: 0.0,
807:                 };
808:                 let mut local_env = env_for_handler.clone();
809:                 local_env.insert(event);
810:                 call_boxed_action(&action_for_handler, &local_env);
811:                 gesture.set_state(gtk4::EventSequenceState::Claimed);
812:             });
813:             widget.add_controller(rotate);
814:         }
815:         Gesture::Then(then) => {
816:             let armed = Rc::new(RefCell::new(false));
817:             let first_action: Rc<RefCell<BoxedAction<()>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Box::new({
818:                 let armed = armed.clone();
819:                 move |_env: &Environment| {
820:                     *armed.borrow_mut() = true;
821:                 }
822:             })));
823:             let second_action: Rc<RefCell<BoxedAction<()>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Box::new({
824:                 let chained_action = action.clone();
825:                 move |env: &Environment| {
826:                     if !*armed.borrow() {
827:                         return;
828:                     }
829:                     *armed.borrow_mut() = false;
830:                     call_boxed_action(&chained_action, env);
831:                 }
832:             })));
833:             install_gesture_observer(widget, then.first().clone(), first_action, env.clone());

1: //! View dispatching infrastructure for `WaterUI` backends.
2: //!
3: //! The [`ViewDispatcher`] maps views to backend-specific handlers based on
4: //! their concrete types. The [`dispatch`](ViewDispatcher::dispatch) method
5: //! provides a zero-allocation generic path where views stay on the stack
6: //! and are passed via `&mut dyn Any` downcast.
7: 
8: use core::any::type_name;
9: use core::fmt;
10: use core::{
11:     any::{Any, TypeId},
12:     fmt::Debug,
13: };
14: use std::cell::Cell;

19: /// Handler that accepts a stack-allocated view via `&mut dyn Any` (`Option<V>` slot).
20: type RawHandlerFn<T, C, R> = Box<dyn Fn(&mut T, C, &mut dyn Any, &Environment) -> R>;
21: 
22: /// Handler that accepts a boxed `AnyView` (for when the view is already type-erased).
23: type BoxedHandlerFn<T, C, R> = Box<dyn Fn(&mut T, C, AnyView, &Environment) -> R>;
24: 
25: /// Holds both dispatch paths for a single registered view type.
26: struct HandlerEntry<T, C, R> {
27:     /// For zero-alloc dispatch: takes `&mut dyn Any` (`Option<V>` slot on stack).
28:     raw: RawHandlerFn<T, C, R>,
29:     /// For `AnyView` dispatch: takes `AnyView`, downcasts to `V`, calls handler.
30:     boxed: BoxedHandlerFn<T, C, R>,
31: }

33: /// A dispatcher that routes views to type-specific handlers.
34: ///
35: /// Backends register handlers for concrete view types (e.g., `Native<TextConfig>`).
36: /// When dispatching a view, the dispatcher:
37: /// 1. Looks up a handler by the view's `TypeId`
38: /// 2. If found, invokes the handler
39: /// 3. If not found, calls `body()` on the view and recurses
40: ///
41: /// # Type Parameters
42: ///
43: /// - `T`: State type owned by the dispatcher
44: /// - `C`: Context type passed to handlers (e.g., parent widget)
45: /// - `R`: Return type from handlers (e.g., created widget)
46: ///
47: /// # Example
48: ///
49: /// ```ignore
50: /// let mut dispatcher: ViewDispatcher<(), GtkContext, gtk4::Widget> = ViewDispatcher::new();
51: ///
52: /// dispatcher.register::<Native<TextConfig>>(|state, ctx, config, env| {
53: ///     let label = gtk4::Label::new(Some(&config.content.get().to_plain()));
54: ///     label.upcast()
55: /// });
56: ///
57: /// let widget = dispatcher.dispatch(my_view, &env, ctx);
58: /// ```
59: pub struct ViewDispatcher<T, C, R> {
60:     state: T,
61:     handlers: HashMap<TypeId, HandlerEntry<T, C, R>>,
62: }
63: 
64: impl<T: Default, C, R> Default for ViewDispatcher<T, C, R> {
65:     fn default() -> Self {
66:         Self::new()
67:     }

116:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
117:         write!(
118:             f,
119:             "ViewDispatcher<{}, {}, {}>(handlers: {})",
120:             type_name::<T>(),
121:             type_name::<C>(),
122:             type_name::<R>(),
123:             self.handlers.len()
124:         )
125:     }
126: }

128: impl<T, C, R> ViewDispatcher<T, C, R> {
129:     /// Creates a new dispatcher with the provided state.
130:     pub fn with_state(state: T) -> Self {
131:         Self {
132:             state,
133:             handlers: HashMap::new(),
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:     /// Returns a reference to the dispatcher's state.
138:     #[must_use]
139:     pub const fn state(&self) -> &T {
140:         &self.state
141:     }
142: 
143:     /// Returns a mutable reference to the dispatcher's state.
144:     pub const fn state_mut(&mut self) -> &mut T {
145:         &mut self.state
146:     }
147: 
148:     /// Registers a handler for a specific view type.
149:     ///
150:     /// # Panics
151:     ///
152:     /// Panics if the internal erased slot does not match the registered view
153:     /// type or if the slot has already been consumed during dispatch.
154:     pub fn register<V: View>(
155:         &mut self,
156:         handler: impl 'static + Clone + Fn(&mut T, C, V, &Environment) -> R,
157:     ) {
158:         let h_raw = handler.clone();
159:         let h_boxed = handler;
160: 
161:         let entry = HandlerEntry {
162:             raw: Box::new(move |state, ctx, slot: &mut dyn Any, env| {
163:                 let v = slot
164:                     .downcast_mut::<Option<V>>()
165:                     .expect("type mismatch in raw dispatch")
166:                     .take()
167:                     .expect("view already taken from slot");
168:                 h_raw(state, ctx, v, env)
169:             }),
170:             boxed: Box::new(move |state, ctx, view: AnyView, env| {
171:                 let v = *view
172:                     .downcast::<V>()
173:                     .expect("type mismatch in boxed dispatch");
174:                 h_boxed(state, ctx, v, env)
175:             }),
176:         };
177:         self.handlers.insert(TypeId::of::<V>(), entry);
178:     }
179: 
180:     /// Dispatches a view to its registered handler.
181:     ///
182:     /// For concrete types: zero-allocation — the view stays on the stack.
183:     /// For `AnyView`: the inner type is inspected and the boxed path is used.
184:     ///
185:     /// If no handler is found, `body()` is called and the result is dispatched
186:     /// recursively.
187:     ///
188:     /// # Panics
189:     ///
190:     /// Panics if an `AnyView` cannot be recovered from the erased dispatch slot.
191:     pub fn dispatch<V: View>(&mut self, view: V, env: &Environment, context: C) -> R {
192:         let tid = TypeId::of::<V>();
193: 
194:         let debug_enabled = std::env::var_os("WATERUI_DISPATCH_DEBUG").is_some();
195:         let _trace_guard = DispatchTraceGuard::enter(debug_enabled, type_name::<V>());
196: 
197:         // AnyView is already heap-allocated — unwrap it and dispatch by inner TypeId.
198:         if tid == TypeId::of::<AnyView>() {
199:             // Extract the AnyView from the generic V via Any downcast.
200:             let mut slot = Some(view);
201:             let any_view = (&mut slot as &mut dyn Any)
202:                 .downcast_mut::<Option<AnyView>>()
203:                 .expect("AnyView downcast should succeed")
204:                 .take()
205:                 .expect("AnyView option should contain a value");
206: 
207:             return self.dispatch_boxed(any_view, env, context);
208:         }
209: 
210:         // Try handler (view stays on stack, downcast via &mut dyn Any)
211:         if let Some(entry) = self.handlers.get(&tid) {
212:             let mut slot: Option<V> = Some(view);
213:             return (entry.raw)(&mut self.state, context, &mut slot as &mut dyn Any, env);
214:         }
215: 
216:         // No handler found: expand body() and recurse — monomorphized, zero allocation
217:         self.dispatch_boxed(AnyView::new(view.body(env)), env, context)
218:     }
219: 
220:     /// Internal: dispatches an already-boxed `AnyView` by its inner `TypeId`.
221:     fn dispatch_boxed(&mut self, view: AnyView, env: &Environment, context: C) -> R {
222:         let debug_enabled = std::env::var_os("WATERUI_DISPATCH_DEBUG").is_some();
223:         let _trace_guard = DispatchTraceGuard::enter(debug_enabled, view.name());
224:         let type_id = view.type_id();
225: 
226:         // AnyView::new() guarantees no nesting — no unwrap check needed.
227: 
228:         if let Some(entry) = self.handlers.get(&type_id) {
229:             (entry.boxed)(&mut self.state, context, view, env)
230:         } else {
231:             // body() returns impl View which AnyView::new wraps back into AnyView
232:             self.dispatch_boxed(AnyView::new(view.body(env)), env, context)
233:         }
234:     }
235: 
236:     /// Returns the number of registered handlers.
237:     #[must_use]
238:     pub fn handler_count(&self) -> usize {
239:         self.handlers.len()
240:     }
241: }

7: /// A wrapper for platform-specific native UI components.

10: /// The generic parameter `T` represents the platform-specific component type.
11: ///
12: /// # Panics

15: /// to be handled by platform-specific rendering backends.

17: pub struct Native<T: NativeView> {
18:     native: T,
19:     fallback: Option<AnyView>,
20: }

22: impl<T: NativeView> Native<T> {
23:     /// Creates a new `Native<T>` view wrapping the given native component.
24:     ///
25:     /// # Arguments
26:     ///
27:     /// * `native` - The platform-specific native UI component to wrap.
28:     pub const fn new(native: T) -> Self {
29:         Self {
30:             native,
31:             fallback: None,
32:         }
33:     }

36:     ///

39:     #[must_use]
40:     pub fn with_fallback(mut self, fallback: impl View) -> Self {
41:         self.fallback = Some(AnyView::new(fallback));
42:         self
43:     }
44: 
45:     /// Consumes the wrapper and returns the inner native component.
46:     #[must_use]
47:     pub fn into_inner(self) -> T {
48:         self.native
49:     }
50:

55:     }
56:

3: //! # Logical Pixels (Points)
4: //!
5: //! All layout values in `WaterUI` use **logical pixels** (also called "points" or "dp").
6: //! This is the same unit system used by design tools like Figma, Sketch, and Adobe XD,
7: //! allowing seamless translation from design to implementation.

9: //! - **1 logical pixel** = 1 point in design tools

1: //! Stack-based layout primitives.
2: //!
3: //! The submodules implement horizontal, vertical, and overlay stacks. These
4: //! views arrange child content according to alignments and spacing and are the
5: //! backbone of most declarative layouts in `WaterUI`.
6: //!
7: //! ![Stack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/water-rs/waterui/dev/docs/illustrations/stack.svg)
8: 
9: /// Emits `for_each` on a stack wrapper around `ForEach<C, F, V>`.
10: ///
11: /// Reused by HStack/VStack/ZStack so the three families share a single
12: /// implementation without exposing a trait users would have to import.
13: /// The macro is private to this crate (no `#[macro_export]`) and is
14: /// invoked at the call site in each stack module.
15: macro_rules! impl_stack_for_each {
16:     ($Stack:ident, $Layout:ident) => {
17:         impl<C, F, V> $Stack<ForEach<C, F, V>>
18:         where
19:             C: Collection,
20:             C::Item: Identifiable,
21:             F: 'static + Fn(C::Item) -> V,
22:             V: View,
23:         {
24:             /// Creates the stack by iterating over a collection and generating
25:             /// views.
26:             pub fn for_each(collection: C, generator: F) -> Self {
27:                 Self {
28:                     layout: $Layout::default(),
29:                     contents: ForEach::new(collection, generator),
30:                 }
31:             }
32:         }
33:     };
34: }

51: /// Defines the axis of a stack.
52: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
53: #[non_exhaustive]
54: pub enum Axis {
55:     /// Horizontal axis is the x-axis (`HStack`)
56:     Horizontal,
57:     /// Vertical axis is the y-axis (`VStack`)
58:     Vertical,
59: }
60: 
61: impl Axis {
62:     /// Returns true if this axis is horizontal.
63:     #[must_use]
64:     pub const fn is_horizontal(&self) -> bool {
65:         matches!(self, Self::Horizontal)
66:     }
67: 
68:     /// Returns true if this axis is vertical.
69:     #[must_use]
70:     pub const fn is_vertical(&self) -> bool {
71:         matches!(self, Self::Vertical)
72:     }
73: }
74: 
75: /// The axis a [`LazyContainer`](crate::container::LazyContainer) can be
76: /// virtualized along, together with the spacing and cross-axis alignment the
77: /// stack was configured with.
78: ///
79: /// Only the two stacks scroll in one direction with a well-defined item order,
80: /// which is what viewport virtualization needs; every other layout — a grid, a
81: /// `ZStack`, an absolute overlay — lays out its whole membership and returns
82: /// `None` here.
83: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
84: pub enum LazyStackAxis {
85:     /// Items run top to bottom, aligned horizontally.
86:     Vertical {
87:         /// Gap between consecutive items.
88:         spacing: Computed<f32>,
89:         /// How items line up across the axis.
90:         alignment: HorizontalAlignment,
91:     },
92:     /// Items run leading to trailing, aligned vertically.
93:     Horizontal {
94:         /// Gap between consecutive items.
95:         spacing: Computed<f32>,
96:         /// How items line up across the axis.
97:         alignment: VerticalAlignment,
98:     },
99: }
100: 
101: /// Resolves a layout to the axis a lazy container can virtualize along.
102: ///
103: /// Every renderer that virtualizes a lazy container asks this, so the answer is
104: /// the same everywhere. Deriving it per backend is how GTK ended up reading
105: /// `Layout::stretch_axis` — a different question entirely, and one whose answer
106: /// changed when the stacks became content-sized, silently laying every lazy
107: /// horizontal stack out vertically.
108: #[must_use]
109: pub fn lazy_stack_axis(layout: &dyn Layout) -> Option<LazyStackAxis> {
110:     let layout = layout as &dyn core::any::Any;
111:     if let Some(vstack) = layout.downcast_ref::<VStackLayout>() {
112:         return Some(LazyStackAxis::Vertical {
113:             spacing: vstack.spacing.clone(),
114:             alignment: vstack.alignment,
115:         });
116:     }
117:     if let Some(hstack) = layout.downcast_ref::<HStackLayout>() {
118:         return Some(LazyStackAxis::Horizontal {
119:             spacing: hstack.spacing.clone(),
120:             alignment: hstack.alignment,
121:         });
122:     }
123:     None
124: }

content.text:
Done. Two commits landed on `feature/pathland-waterui-backend`:

**1. `ec77665` — Phase 1 (split):** `pathland-core` is now pure protocol; the emitter moved to `pathland-engine`.

**2. `36ed115` — Phase 2 (backend crate):** new `pathland-waterui/` crate with a working round-trip.

## What I learned (resolved the three research items)

- **Traversal**: WaterUI views reach a backend as `Native<Config>` leaf types (via `raw_view!`/`configurable!`); composites auto-expand through `View::body`. The canonical mechanism is `ViewDispatcher`, but a hand-rolled `AnyView` walker suffices for a fixed catalog.
- **Stack axis**: `vstack`/`hstack` inject an `Axis` into the `Environment` via `Metadata<Environment>` — that's how you tell VStack from HStack (the underlying `VStackLayout`/`HStackLayout` is hidden behind a private `DirectionalLayout`).
- **Reactivity**: `nami` `Signal`/`Computed` with `.watch()`; guards are kept alive via `Metadata<Retain>`.

## What's built

- `producer.rs` — `Emitter`: walks the view tree, emits `CREATE_NODE`/`INSERT_CHILD`/`SET_TEXT` for `FixedContainer`/`TextConfig`/`Spacer`, unwraps `Metadata<Environment>`/`Metadata<Retain>`.
- `consumer.rs` — `Consumer`: applies `Frame`s into a retained `id → {component, text, properties, children}` map (no platform widget).
- `tests/roundtrip.rs` — `vstack((text("hello"), text("world")))` → opcodes → decoded back to VSTACK + 2 TEXT nodes; HStack axis detected too. **2/2 green.**

## Notes & known gaps for the next increment

- The crate lives **outside** `lib/rust` (own workspace) because WaterUI is edition 2024; deps are path-based to the sibling `../../waterui` checkout.
- Spacing/alignment aren't extracted yet (hidden behind `DirectionalLayout`); text/container/spacer structure round-trips already.
- Reactivity (`Binding`/`Computed` → `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT` deltas) and the consumer's `rebuild()` back into real WaterUI views are the natural next step, followed by Phase 4's macOS demo.

Want me to continue with reactivity + more component types, or move to wiring up the consumer's `rebuild()` and the Phase 4 Apple-backend demo?
Yeah

content.text:
Done. Button + spacing are in, and all 6 tests pass with no warnings.

## What changed

**`pathland-waterui`** (committed as `26c6895`):
- **Producer** now emits `BUTTON` (label extracted via `Label::accessibility_label()`, reactive `SET_TEXT` delta via the shared leaf path) and `SPACING` for stacks (axis + spacing read from a new accessor).
- **Consumer** rebuilds `Button` and honors `SPACING` when reconstructing `VStack`/`HStack`.
- New tests: `button_round_trips`, `spacing_is_emitted`.

**WaterUI** (separate local checkout change, not part of the Pathland commit): added `FixedContainer::stack_axis()` to `components/foundation/layout/src/containers/container.rs` — it unwraps the private `DirectionalLayout` and delegates to the existing `lazy_stack_axis`, so the fixed (non-lazy) stack path can expose its axis/spacing. This is the "small WaterUI accessor" from earlier; it lives in your `~/Development/michaelkrog/waterui` checkout, so keep it or upstream it.

## Coverage now

| WaterUI | Pathland opcodes |
|---|---|
| `vstack`/`hstack` | `VSTACK`/`HSTACK` + `SPACING` |
| `text` | `TEXT` + `SET_TEXT` (reactive) |
| `button` | `BUTTON` + `SET_TEXT` (reactive) |
| `spacer` | `SPACER` |

Round-trip (emit → decode → rebuild → re-emit) is lossless for this subset; reactive `SET_TEXT` deltas work.

Next options: (a) reactive `SPACING`/property deltas (extend the leaf-subscription mechanism to `SET_PROPERTY`), (b) more component types, or (c) move to the Phase 4 macOS demo. Which would you like?

1: //! Producer: walk a WaterUI view tree and emit Pathland opcodes.
2: //!
3: //! The emitter owns a [`RingTransport`] and walks the view tree with a
4: //! hand-rolled recursive walker over [`AnyView`]. It handles the raw native
5: //! leaf types it knows about (container, text, spacer) and unwraps the two
6: //! metadata wrappers WaterUI uses to smuggle state past the type-erasure
7: //! boundary (`Metadata<Environment>` for the stack axis, `Metadata<Retain>`
8: //! for watcher-guard lifetimes). Any other view is a composite and is expanded
9: //! via [`View::body`].
10: //!
11: //! Reactive text is the one piece of change detection the producer participates
12: //! in: a [`TextConfig`] carries a [`Computed`] content signal, so the emitter
13: //! subscribes to it and re-emits a `SET_TEXT` delta for that node whenever it
14: //! changes. Everything else is WaterUI's job.
15: 
16: use std::cell::RefCell;
17: use std::rc::Rc;
18: 
19: use pathland_core::{component_type, property_id, value_type, Guest, RingError};
20: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
21: use waterui_controls::button::ButtonConfig;
22: use waterui_core::reactive::watcher::BoxWatcherGuard;
23: use waterui_core::{AnyView, Computed, Environment, Metadata, Native, Retain, Signal, View};
24: use waterui_layout::container::FixedContainer;
25: use waterui_layout::spacer::Spacer;
26: use waterui_layout::stack::{Axis, LazyStackAxis};
27: use waterui_text::TextConfig;
28: use waterui_text::styled::StyledStr;
29: 
30: /// Sentinel parent id for the root node (the ring treats `0` as "no parent").
31: const ROOT_PARENT: u32 = 0;
32: 
33: /// A reactive text binding: node id + its live content signal.
34: type ReactiveText = (u32, Computed<StyledStr>);
35: 
36: /// Emits WaterUI views as Pathland opcodes into a shared-memory ring.
37: pub struct Emitter {
38:     transport: Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>,
39:     next_id: u32,
40:     guards: Vec<BoxWatcherGuard>,
41: }
42: 
43: impl Default for Emitter {
44:     fn default() -> Self {
45:         Self::new()
46:     }
47: }
48: 
49: impl Emitter {
50:     /// Create an emitter owning a fresh shared-memory ring.
51:     #[must_use]
52:     pub fn new() -> Self {
53:         Self {
54:             transport: Rc::new(RefCell::new(RingTransport::new())),
55:             next_id: 1,
56:             guards: Vec::new(),
57:         }
58:     }
59: 
60:     /// The shared ring, for consumers that read frames in place.
61:     #[must_use]
62:     pub fn transport(&self) -> Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>> {
63:         Rc::clone(&self.transport)
64:     }
65: 
66:     /// Emit a view as one frame, returning the id of the root node.
67:     ///
68:     /// Reactive text fields found during the walk are subscribed to so that a
69:     /// later signal change emits a `SET_TEXT` delta for the affected node.
70:     pub fn emit<V: View>(&mut self, view: V, env: &Environment) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
71:         let mut reactive: Vec<ReactiveText> = Vec::new();
72: 
73:         let (root, next_id) = {
74:             let transport = Rc::clone(&self.transport);
75:             let mut borrow = transport.borrow_mut();
76:             let mut guest = borrow.producer();
77:             guest.begin_frame();
78: 
79:             let (root, next_id) = {
80:                 let mut walk = Walk {
81:                     guest: &mut guest,
82:                     next_id: self.next_id,
83:                     reactive: &mut reactive,
84:                 };
85:                 let root = walk.any(AnyView::new(view), env, ROOT_PARENT)?;
86:                 (root, walk.next_id)
87:             };
88: 
89:             guest.end_frame();
90:             (root, next_id)
91:         };
92:         self.next_id = next_id;
93: 
94:         for (node_id, content) in reactive {
95:             let transport = Rc::clone(&self.transport);
96:             let guard = content.watch(move |ctx| {
97:                 let text = ctx.into_value().to_plain().to_string();
98:                 let mut borrow = transport.borrow_mut();
99:                 let mut guest = borrow.producer();
100:                 guest.begin_frame();
101:                 let _ = guest.set_text(node_id, &text);
102:                 guest.end_frame();
103:             });
104:             self.guards.push(Box::new(guard));
105:         }
106: 
107:         Ok(root)
108:     }
109: }

111: /// The recursive walker: borrows the guest ring plus the reactive sink, and owns
112: /// the node-id cursor for the duration of one emit pass.
113: struct Walk<'g, 'm> {
114:     guest: &'g mut Guest<'m>,
115:     next_id: u32,
116:     reactive: &'g mut Vec<ReactiveText>,
117: }

136:         if view.is::<Metadata<Environment>>() {

content.text:
Done. Reactive property deltas are in (commit `2b03910`), 7 tests green, no warnings.

## What changed

Generalized the reactive subscription from text-only to a `Reactive` enum:

- `Reactive::Text { node, content }` → `SET_TEXT` delta on change
- `Reactive::Property { node, property, value }` → `SET_PROPERTY` delta (F32) on change

The stack's `spacing: Computed<f32>` now subscribes and re-emits `SET_PROPERTY(SPACING)` when it changes — verified by `reactive_spacing_emits_delta` (8.0 → 24.0).

## Current state

| WaterUI | Pathland | Reactive |
|---|---|---|
| `vstack`/`hstack` | `VSTACK`/`HSTACK` + `SPACING` | spacing ✓ |
| `text` | `TEXT` + `SET_TEXT` | ✓ |
| `button` | `BUTTON` + `SET_TEXT` | ✓ |
| `spacer` | `SPACER` | — |

The `Reactive` enum makes it easy to add more property types (opacity, color, etc.) by adding a variant. Round-trip losslessness and reactive deltas both hold.

Remaining options: more property/component coverage, or the Phase 4 macOS demo (Apple backend). What next?
Which do you recommend?

content.text:
Demo scaffolded and committed (`d0c1c8e`). Here's the state and what's blocking a full run.

## What's there

`examples/pathland-roundtrip/` — a WaterUI playground:

- `src/lib.rs` — `main()` authors a `vstack` of `text`/`spacer`/`button`, then runs it through `Emitter` → `Consumer::rebuild()` and returns the reconstruction for the Apple backend to render. `waterui_ffi::export!()` gives the C entry points AppKit calls.
- `Cargo.toml` — `waterui` (gpu **disabled**; AppKit needs no wgpu/Metal) + `waterui-ffi` (gpu disabled) + `pathland-waterui` + `pathland-core-transport`, all via path.
- `Water.toml` — `type = "playground"`, `waterui_path` pointing at your local checkout.

The round-trip logic is the exact `emit → decode → rebuild` path already proven by the 7 `pathland-waterui` tests.

## Two environment blockers (pre-existing, would block *any* WaterUI macOS app here)

1. **Metal Toolchain not installed** — `waterui-ffi` unconditionally pulls `waterui-media`/`waterui-video` → `waterui-graphics`, whose build script compiles `.wgsl` shaders to Metal. Fix:
   ```
   xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain
   ```

2. **Swift toolchain mismatch** — `swift` resolves to swiftly's Swift 6.1 (`~/.swiftly/bin/swift`), but the WaterKit build needs Xcode's Swift 6.3.3. I verified prepending Xcode's toolchain fixes this (the error then advances from Swift to the Metal one):
   ```
   export PATH="/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/bin:$PATH"
   ```
   Run `water run --platform macos` with that PATH (or fix swiftly's default toolchain).

Once both are resolved, `cd examples/pathland-roundtrip && water run --platform macos` should render the reconstructed view natively.

Want me to (a) install the Metal toolchain now (it's a large Xcode component download), (b) continue adding property/component coverage while the environment is sorted, or (c) leave it here?
I fixed both but it still does not fully compile

24: fn roundtrip(view: impl View) -> AnyView {
25:     let env = Environment::new();

27:     let mut emitter = Emitter::new();

33:         let mut borrow = transport.borrow_mut();

35:             consumer.apply(batch.frame());
36:         }
37:     }

content.text:
Done. Single app logic, backend chosen at run time (commit `44a1eeb`).

## Structure

- `src/roundtrip.rs` — the **one app logic**: `source()` authors the view, `roundtrip()` emits opcodes and decodes them for both renderers.
- `src/lib.rs` — macOS entry point: `main()` returns the native reconstruction.
- `src/bin/html.rs` — HTML entry point: prints the HTML document to the console.

## Running

```
water run --platform macos   # native (AppKit)
cargo run --bin html         # HTML → console
```

Verified both: `water run --platform macos` → "Application started"; `cargo run --bin html` prints the full HTML document (flex column/row, spans, `flex:1` spacer, buttons).

## One note on `--platform html`

`water` CLI's `--platform` only accepts real run targets (`ios`/`android`/`macos`/`linux`/`web`…), and those all build/launch a GUI app through a WaterUI backend. "HTML → console" isn't a GUI app, so it doesn't fit that model — it's a plain console binary, hence `cargo run --bin html`.

If you'd rather have a literal `water run --platform html`, that means teaching the water CLI a new platform (build → run a console binary), which is a change to WaterUI's own CLI — I can do that, but it's a larger, separate effort. Want me to pursue that, or is `cargo run --bin html` sufficient?

Is watterui over pathland to macos renderer zero-copy all the way?

Short answer: **no — not end-to-end.** Only one hop is zero-copy (the ring itself). The WaterUI bridge at *both* ends copies text and allocates trees. Here's the actual data path in the demo:

## Where it IS zero-copy

The `RingTransport` → `Frame` hop. The producer writes 16-byte opcodes into a shared ring; the consumer reads them **in place** — `Frame::opcodes()` and `Frame::arena_str()` borrow the ring memory, no serialization/re-parse. That's Pathland's transport guarantee, and it holds.

## Where it copies

Text (`"Pathland round-trip"`, `"Hello"`, …) is copied at least **5 times**:

| # | Where | Copy |
|---|-------|------|
| 1 | `emit_leaf` (`producer.rs`) | `content.get().to_plain().to_string()` — `Computed<StyledStr>` → `String` |
| 2 | `emit_leaf` | `guest.set_text(id, &text)` — `String` → arena bytes |
| 3 | `Consumer::apply_style` | `arena_str()` borrows (free) → `.to_string()` into `Node.text` |
| 4 | `Consumer::rebuild` | `node.text.clone()` |
| 5 | `Text::new` → `TextConfig` | `String` → `StyledStr` inside `Computed` |
| 6 | Apple backend FFI | `WuiStr` → Swift `String` → native `NSTextField` |

The *structure* isn't zero-copy either: decode materializes a `BTreeMap<u32, Node>` (heap alloc per node), then `rebuild()` constructs a **fresh** WaterUI view tree from scratch.

## Why it's inherent

The bridge is converting between two different representations at each boundary:

- **Producer**: WaterUI's `Computed<StyledStr>` (rich, styled, reactive) has no way to be *placed* into Pathland's arena without flattening it to a plain `String`.
- **Consumer**: `rebuild()` must *own* `String`s (and `AnyView`s) to construct fresh WaterUI views — it can't borrow the arena, because the reconstructed views outlive the frame and must be `'static`.

So each serialization/deserialization forces a copy of text, plus two tree allocations (retained map + rebuilt views).

## Contrast with Pathland's real zero-copy path

The **desktop** path (`pathland-view-native` → `pathland-render-gtk`) is genuinely zero-copy: the renderer's `RenderTree` reads `Frame` borrowing the ring and maps `id → gtk::Widget` directly, without materializing a second description tree or copying strings out of the arena (it borrows them). The WaterUI bridge is *less* zero-copy because WaterUI's renderer consumes WaterUI `View` values, not the opcode stream — so the consumer must re-materialize views.

Net: the **protocol/transport layer is zero-copy; the WaterUI bridge at each end is not**, and the round-trip demo sits in the copy-heavy middle. If the goal were to maximize zero-copy, the lever is the consumer — avoid `rebuild()` and instead have a renderer that applies `Frame`s directly to native widgets (like `pathland-render-gtk`), rather than reconstructing WaterUI views. Good questions — they get at the actual distinction between the two frameworks.

## 1. Is WaterUI itself zero-copy?

No, not in the sense you're using the term — and "zero-copy" isn't the right lens for it anyway.

WaterUI's FFI is a **function-call C ABI**, not a shared-memory ring. Data crosses the boundary by calling `waterui_*` functions. Some of it is zero-copy by design:

- **Arrays/strings** are `WuiArray`/`WuiStr` — *"zero-copy views into Rust data via vtable-based slicing"* (the FFI README's words). The Swift side borrows the bytes rather than the Rust side copying them out first.
- **Reactive updates** are *"direct function pointer callbacks, no allocation"*.

But it's not zero-copy in the Pathland sense: there's no shared ring/arena, the config structs are marshaled across the boundary, and — the part that's unavoidable everywhere — **the native widget ends up owning its own copy of the string** (`NSTextField.stringValue = …` materializes a Swift `String`).

The honest summary: WaterUI optimizes for **fine-grained updates and native widgets**, not for "no copies." Pathland optimizes for **language-agnostic transport + a zero-copy shared ring**. They're different axes; you can't point at one and ask "is it zero-copy?" without saying zero-copy *of what*.

## 2. If it's pull-based and traverses a tree, how is change detection fine-grained?

Because **the traversal is not change detection — it's construction.** The two phases are orthogonal:

- **Build phase (pull)**: the backend walks the tree once, calls `body()` recursively, creates native widgets — and, crucially, for each reactive field it encounters (a `Binding`/`Computed` in a `TextConfig`, a `Button` label, etc.) it **subscribes a watcher** (`waterui_watch_binding_*` → a function-pointer callback).

- **Update phase (push)**: when you `binding.set(...)`, `nami`'s signal graph fires **only the watchers subscribed to that exact signal**. Each watcher is a direct callback into the backend that mutates **one widget property** (`label.text = newValue`). No tree walk, no diff, no re-`body()`.

So WaterUI is **pull to construct, push to update**. The AGENTS.md states it directly: *"There is no virtual tree to diff, and changing one string never rebuilds the subtree around it."* That's what "fine-grained" means — the update path is a signal → subscription graph, not a tree traversal. The tree is only re-walked for *structural* changes (`when`/`watch`/`ForEach` membership), which is deliberate.

## Why this matters for your earlier question

This actually sharpens the "apply frames directly" idea. WaterUI's native backends *already* apply deltas directly — via signal watchers — they just don't use a serialized stream. What Pathland adds is a **transportable, serialized form of those same deltas** (the `Frame`), so they can cross a process/language boundary. The copies you saw in the demo are the cost of that serialization+deserialization layer, not of WaterUI's change-detection model.

So the cleanest framing of your goal is: **feed Pathland's serialized deltas into WaterUI's existing push-update machinery (signals), rather than reconstructing a view tree.** That's exactly the "incremental `id → Native<Config>` + per-node `Binding`" option — it reuses WaterUI's fine-grained watchers as the *destination* of Pathland's frames, instead of `rebuild()`.

That's a cleaner direction, and it matches Pathland's original Goal #15 (the Quarkus SSR + WebSocket target). Native should stay native — WaterUI's Apple/GTK backends are already the right tool there, and round-tripping native through opcodes buys nothing but the copies we just spent two messages talking about. Pathland becomes the **web projection layer**: WaterUI tree → opcodes → browser.

## What that means for the existing code

| Piece | Fate |
|---|---|
| `pathland-waterui` **producer** (`Emitter`: view → opcodes) | Keep — this is the app→wire bridge |
| `pathland-render-html` | Keep + extend — this *is* the SSR renderer |
| `pathland-core-transport` (network batch + event ring) | Keep — this is the **hybrid** machinery (WebSocket deltas + input) |
| `pathland-waterui` **consumer** (opcodes → WaterUI views) | Demote to a test-only "lossless round-trip" check; native no longer uses it |
| Demo | Native `main()` returns `source()` directly; web path = SSR (existing `html` bin), later served/streamed |

## SSR / CSR / hybrid, concretely

- **SSR** — a server runs `source()` → opcodes → `pathland-render-html` → serve HTML. No browser runtime, no native backend needed. ~80% already built.
- **Hybrid** — SSR the first paint, then stream opcode-delta batches over WebSocket and feed input back through the event ring. This is where the protocol's *delta* value shines (fine-grained updates over a wire). The transport crate already has `BatchEncoder`/`Batcher` + `RingTransport` + the event ring.
- **CSR** — the app compiles to WASM, emits opcodes into WASM linear memory, a JS/WIT host reads the ring and mutates the DOM. Most work, and it overlaps WaterUI's own web target (Hydrolysis), so it's the least differentiated.

## Recommendation

**SSR first, then hybrid.** SSR finishes the web story with almost no new code and is the natural end-to-end proof; hybrid adds the interactivity that makes the protocol earn its keep. Defer CSR.

One honest caveat to flag: for *pure* SSR the opcode protocol is arguably unnecessary — you could walk the view tree server-side and emit HTML directly. The protocol's real payoff is **hybrid** (incremental deltas) and cross-language/cross-process. Using it for SSR is fine as a uniform first step that sets up hybrid, but worth knowing it's not strictly required there.

## Questions

1. **Server runtime** — a small Rust server (axum/actix, trivial since everything is already Rust), or Quarkus/Java (the original Goal #15, which needs a *Java* opcode→HTML renderer — a much bigger lift)?
2. **Native now** — confirm the macOS/GTK demos drop Pathland entirely (`main()` returns the view directly), with Pathland only reachable via the SSR/HTML path?
3. **Scope for this pass** — just re-scope the repo + finish SSR, or also start hybrid (WebSocket delta streaming + event round-trip)?

128: /// Build a pointer-opcode flags word from the pointer/hover bits.
129: #[inline]
130: fn flag_for(secondary: bool, hovering: bool, leaving: bool) -> u16 {
131:     let mut flags = 0u16;
132:     if secondary {
133:         flags |= flag::POINTER_SECONDARY;
134:     }
135:     if hovering {
136:         flags |= flag::HOVER_ENTER;
137:     }
138:     if leaving {
139:         flags |= flag::HOVER_LEAVE;
140:     }
141:     flags
142: }

144: /// Error decoding a raw-input event from an opcode.
145: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
146: pub enum EventError {
147:     /// The opcode is not an `EVENT` category opcode.
148:     NotAnEvent,
149:     /// The opcode is an EVENT category opcode but an unknown command.
150:     UnknownCommand,
151: }

153: impl TryFrom<Opcode> for Event {
154:     type Error = EventError;

156:     fn try_from(op: Opcode) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
157:         if op.category() != category::EVENT {

160:         let flags = op.flags();
161:         match op.command() {
162:             crate::event::POINTER_DOWN => Ok(Event::PointerDown {
163:                 target: op.a(),
164:                 x: op.b_f32(),
165:                 y: op.c_f32(),
166:                 secondary: flags & flag::POINTER_SECONDARY != 0,
167:             }),
168:             crate::event::POINTER_MOVE => Ok(Event::PointerMove {
169:                 target: op.a(),
170:                 x: op.b_f32(),
171:                 y: op.c_f32(),
172:                 hovering: flags & flag::HOVER_ENTER != 0,
173:                 leaving: flags & flag::HOVER_LEAVE != 0,
174:             }),
175:             crate::event::POINTER_UP => Ok(Event::PointerUp {
176:                 target: op.a(),
177:                 x: op.b_f32(),
178:                 y: op.c_f32(),
179:                 secondary: flags & flag::POINTER_SECONDARY != 0,
180:             }),
181:             crate::event::KEY_DOWN => Ok(Event::KeyDown {
182:                 target: op.a(),
183:                 key_code: op.b() as u16,
184:                 modifiers: op.c() as u8,
185:                 repeat: flags & flag::KEY_REPEAT != 0,
186:             }),
187:             crate::event::KEY_UP => Ok(Event::KeyUp {
188:                 target: op.a(),
189:                 key_code: op.b() as u16,
190:                 modifiers: op.c() as u8,
191:             }),
192:             _ => Err(EventError::UnknownCommand),
193:         }
194:     }
195: }

This is now a clean, coherent direction. Here's the full plan.

## Architecture

```
WaterUI app (Rust)
  ├─ native:  view → Apple/GTK backend (direct — no Pathland)
  └─ web:     view → producer (opcodes)
                 ├─ SSR:    pathland-render-html → HTML document (served)
                 └─ hybrid: BatchEncoder → WebSocket → JS DOM
                            + events (click) → event ring → action → delta
```

The key simplification this unlocks: the web server is a **pure Rust HTTP server** — it depends only on `waterui-core/layout/text/controls` (to author the view) + `pathland-waterui` (producer) + `pathland-render-html` + `pathland-core-transport` + axum/tokio. No `waterui-ffi`, no gpu/vello, no Xcode/Metal/Swift. Plain `cargo run`.

## Phase 1 — Re-scope native

- `examples/pathland-roundtrip/src/lib.rs`: `main()` returns `source()` directly (drop the round-trip).
- **Removal** (recommend deferring until Phase 2–3 prove the web path, then a clean commit): `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-view-native`, `pathland-render-gtk`, `pathland-render-gtk-demo`, `pathland-codegen`, `lib/ui/components.yaml`, `lib/java`, `generate.sh`; update `lib/rust/Cargo.toml`, `check-wasm.sh`, `AGENTS.md`.

## Phase 2 — SSR server (`examples/pathland-web`, axum)

- `src/app.rs` — the WaterUI view (`source()`).
- `src/ssr.rs` — `view → Emitter → HtmlRenderer::render → String`.
- `src/main.rs` — `GET /` serves the HTML document.
- Deps are lightweight (listed above); runs with `cargo run`.

## Phase 3 — Hybrid (WebSocket deltas + events)

- **Producer extension**: expose `(frame_count, opcodes, arena_used)` so `BatchEncoder` can serialize the stream (the ring's `Frame` gives opcodes/arena; the cursor + frame count need exposing). Also capture `ButtonConfig.action` per `node_id` for input dispatch.
- **Push mechanism**: the producer's reactive watchers currently write into a ring; for WebSocket they need to *push* (a channel/wake) so the server forwards deltas instead of polling. This is the main producer refactor.
- **Server**: `GET /ws`; on connect, send the full initial batch; then stream delta batches on state change.
- **Client** (`static/app.js`, ~250 lines): decode the batch wire format (16-byte header + 16-byte opcodes + arena delta, mirrored arena), maintain `nodeId → element`, apply TREE/STYLE deltas to the DOM, send click → `EVENT` opcode → WebSocket.
- **Event round-trip**: add `HOST_TO_GUEST` batches to the transport — the `direction::HOST_TO_GUEST` bit already exists in the wire format, but event batching isn't implemented (the gap the AGENTS.md already flags). This is the one protocol-level change.

Demo interactivity, in two steps: **(a)** timer-driven counter (server-push deltas, no input — proves the WebSocket delta path), then **(b)** button click (full event → action → binding → delta → DOM loop).

## Remaining questions

1. **Removal timing** — drop the native Pathland crates now, or after the web stack works (recommend: after)?
2. **Browser client** — hand-written JS (recommended: demonstrates the language-agnostic protocol), or WASM-compile `pathland-render-html` (DRY but loses the "any language can render" point)?
3. **Hybrid scope** — include the input round-trip (events) in this pass, or land server-push deltas first and add input as a follow-up?
1: After. 2: js that renders directly into documentFragments. 3: Include input as phase 4

All questions resolved. Here's the final plan.

## Overview

Pathland becomes the **web projection layer** (Rust server + JS browser client). Native is pure WaterUI. Deliverables: a lightweight `examples/pathland-web` server crate (SSR → hybrid → input) with a JS client, plus the eventual removal of the native Pathland crates.

```
WaterUI app view
  ├─ native:  → Apple/GTK backend (direct)
  └─ web:     → Emitter (opcodes)
                 ├─ SSR:    HtmlRenderer → HTML (GET /)
                 ├─ hybrid: BatchEncoder → WebSocket → JS (DocumentFragment → DOM)
                 └─ input:  click → EVENT batch → action → Binding → delta
```

## Phase 1 — Re-scope native (small)

- `examples/pathland-roundtrip/src/lib.rs`: `main()` returns the view directly; delete the `roundtrip` module and the `html` bin (the web path moves to the server crate).
- No crate removal yet.

## Phase 2 — SSR server (`examples/pathland-web`, axum + tokio)

- `src/app.rs` — the WaterUI view (the "app logic").
- `src/ssr.rs` — `view → Emitter → HtmlRenderer::render → String`.
- `src/main.rs` — `GET /` serves the HTML document.
- Deps: `waterui-core/layout/text/controls`, `pathland-waterui`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-core-transport`, `axum`, `tokio`. **No gpu/wgpu, no Xcode/Metal/Swift** — plain `cargo run`.

## Phase 3 — Hybrid (WebSocket deltas, server → browser)

- **Producer refactor** (the main one): the `Emitter` today writes reactive deltas into an owned `RingTransport`. For streaming it must instead **push** each frame to a sink (e.g. `mpsc::Sender<Vec<u8>>`), exposing `(frame_count, opcodes, arena_used)` so `BatchEncoder` can serialize. The reactive watchers (text/spacing) call the same push path.
- **Server**: `GET /ws`; on connect, send the full initial batch; then forward delta batches as state changes. App state lives in a single-threaded actor (see below); HTTP/WS layer talks to it over channels.
- **Client** (`static/app.js`): decode the batch wire format (16-byte header + 16-byte opcodes + arena-delta with a mirrored arena), keep `nodeId → element`, apply TREE/STYLE deltas, render the initial batch into a **DocumentFragment** (single insertion) and mutate existing nodes on deltas.
- Demo trigger: timer-driven counter (server-push deltas, no input yet).

## Phase 4 — Input round-trip

- **Transport**: add `HOST_TO_GUEST` event batches (the `direction` bit exists; event batching is the unimplemented gap). Encode `EVENT` opcodes into a batch for the reverse direction.
- **Producer**: capture `ButtonConfig.action` into a `nodeId → action` map.
- **Server actor**: the WaterUI state is `!Send` (bindings/actions), so it runs on a single thread (`tokio::task::LocalSet` or a dedicated thread with a command channel). Incoming clicks → `binding.set(...)` → reactive delta → pushed to the WS.
- **JS**: button `click` → send `EVENT` (PointerUp) over the WebSocket.

## Phase 5 — Removal (after the web stack works)

Delete `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-view-native`, `pathland-render-gtk`, `pathland-render-gtk-demo`, `pathland-codegen`, `lib/ui/components.yaml`, `lib/java`, `generate.sh`; update `lib/rust/Cargo.toml`, `check-wasm.sh`, `AGENTS.md`. The `pathland-waterui` consumer (opcodes → WaterUI views) demotes to a test-only round-trip check.

## Minor decisions to confirm

1. **App-view sharing** — the native demo and the web server both author the same view. Keep them duplicated (simplest), or extract a tiny shared crate (`examples/pathland-app`)? I'd duplicate for now.
2. **Native demo fate** — after re-scope, `pathland-roundtrip` is just a plain WaterUI app. Keep it as the "native twin" of the web demo, or drop it entirely and leave `pathland-web` as the only demo?
3. **HTTP/WS stack** — axum (with `axum::ws`) is my default; any preference?

Ready to execute from Phase 1 when you switch me out of plan mode.
Lets wait with the hybrid approach..  Only SSR for now but still with events and deltas via websocket.

Got it — reframing "hybrid" as **SSR-authoritative with live deltas + events over WebSocket**, and deferring actual CSR/hydration (where the client renders independently). The server stays the single source of truth; the browser is a thin client that applies deltas and reports events.

## Revised architecture

```
WaterUI app view
  ├─ native:  → Apple/GTK backend (direct)
  └─ web:     → Emitter (opcodes)
                 ├─ SSR:   HtmlRenderer → HTML with data-pathland-id (GET /)
                 ├─ deltas: state change → BatchEncoder → WebSocket → JS mutates DOM
                 └─ events: click → EVENT batch (HOST_TO_GUEST) → action → Binding → delta
```

## Phases

**Phase 1 — Re-scope native.** `examples/pathland-roundtrip` returns the view directly; drop its `roundtrip` module + `html` bin (the web path moves to the server crate).

**Phase 2 — SSR + live WebSocket (the whole web stack, this pass).**

- **`pathland-render-html`**: emit a stable `data-pathland-id` on each element so the client can map deltas back to nodes.
- **Producer refactor**: instead of writing reactive deltas into an owned ring, the `Emitter` pushes `(frame_count, opcodes, arena_used)` to a sink (`mpsc`), so `BatchEncoder` can serialize the stream; reactive watchers reuse the same push path. Also capture `ButtonConfig.action` → `nodeId → action`.
- **Server** (`examples/pathland-web`, axum + tokio):
  - A single-threaded **app actor** owns the WaterUI state (bindings/actions are `!Send`) — dedicated thread/`LocalSet` + channels to the HTTP/WS handlers.
  - `GET /` → render current state to HTML (with `data-pathland-id`).
  - `GET /ws` → subscribe to delta broadcasts; forward encoded batches on state change.
  - WS inbound → decode `EVENT` batch → dispatch action → `binding.set` → delta out.
- **Transport**: add `HOST_TO_GUEST` event batches (the `direction` bit exists; event batching is the unimplemented gap).
- **Client** (`static/app.js`): hydrate by scanning `[data-pathland-id]` → `nodeId → element`; apply delta batches (16-byte header + opcodes + mirrored arena); render initial structure into a `DocumentFragment` where needed; send click → `EVENT` (PointerUp) over WS.

**Deferred — CSR/hydration (real "hybrid").** WASM guest, client-side rendering; revisit later.

**Phase 3 — Removal (after the web stack works).** Delete `pathland-engine/view/view-native/render-gtk/render-gtk-demo/codegen`, `lib/ui`, `lib/java`, `generate.sh`; update `lib/rust/Cargo.toml`, `check-wasm.sh`, `AGENTS.md`. Demote the `pathland-waterui` consumer to a test-only round-trip check.

## Key design point worth confirming

Since SSR is authoritative, deltas reference node ids that must match the SSR HTML — hence `data-pathland-id` + client-side hydration. This is the one thing that differs from a pure "client builds from the initial batch" approach. Sound right, or would you rather the server send the full initial batch over WS on connect (client builds the DOM itself, SSR HTML is just first-paint)?

  └─ web:    → Emitter (opcodes)

                └─ events: click → EVENT batch (HOST_TO_GUEST) → action → Binding → delta

1: //! Producer: walk a WaterUI view tree and emit Pathland opcodes.
2: //!
3: //! The emitter owns a [`RingTransport`] and walks the view tree with a
4: //! hand-rolled recursive walker over [`AnyView`]. It handles the raw native
5: //! leaf types it knows about (container, text, spacer) and unwraps the two
6: //! metadata wrappers WaterUI uses to smuggle state past the type-erasure
7: //! boundary (`Metadata<Environment>` for the stack axis, `Metadata<Retain>`
8: //! for watcher-guard lifetimes). Any other view is a composite and is expanded
9: //! via [`View::body`].
10: //!
11: //! Reactive fields are the one piece of change detection the producer
12: //! participates in: a [`TextConfig`] carries a [`Computed`] content signal and
13: //! a stack carries a [`Computed`] spacing signal, so the emitter subscribes to
14: //! each and re-emits a `SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY` delta for that node whenever
15: //! it changes. Everything else is WaterUI's job.
16:

18: use std::rc::Rc;

20: use pathland_core::{component_type, property_id, value_type, Guest, RingError};
21: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
22: use waterui_controls::button::ButtonConfig;
23: use waterui_core::reactive::watcher::BoxWatcherGuard;
24: use waterui_core::{AnyView, Computed, Environment, Metadata, Native, Retain, Signal, View};

31: /// Sentinel parent id for the root node (the ring treats `0` as "no parent").
32: const ROOT_PARENT: u32 = 0;
33: 
34: /// A reactive binding discovered during the walk.
35: enum Reactive {
36:     /// A node's text content, re-emitted as `SET_TEXT`.
37:     Text { node: u32, content: Computed<StyledStr> },
38:     /// A node's `f32` property, re-emitted as `SET_PROPERTY` (`value_type::F32`).
39:     Property { node: u32, property: u16, value: Computed<f32> },
40: }

42: /// Emits WaterUI views as Pathland opcodes into a shared-memory ring.
43: pub struct Emitter {
44:     transport: Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>,
45:     next_id: u32,
46:     guards: Vec<BoxWatcherGuard>,
47: }
48: 
49: impl Default for Emitter {
50:     fn default() -> Self {
51:         Self::new()
52:     }
53: }
54: 
55: impl Emitter {
56:     /// Create an emitter owning a fresh shared-memory ring.
57:     #[must_use]
58:     pub fn new() -> Self {
59:         Self {
60:             transport: Rc::new(RefCell::new(RingTransport::new())),
61:             next_id: 1,
62:             guards: Vec::new(),
63:         }
64:     }
65: 
66:     /// The shared ring, for consumers that read frames in place.
67:     #[must_use]
68:     pub fn transport(&self) -> Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>> {
69:         Rc::clone(&self.transport)
70:     }
71: 
72:     /// Emit a view as one frame, returning the id of the root node.
73:     ///
74:     /// Reactive fields found during the walk are subscribed to so that a later
75:     /// signal change emits a `SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY` delta for the affected
76:     /// node.
77:     pub fn emit<V: View>(&mut self, view: V, env: &Environment) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
78:         let mut reactive: Vec<Reactive> = Vec::new();
79: 
80:         let (root, next_id) = {
81:             let transport = Rc::clone(&self.transport);
82:             let mut borrow = transport.borrow_mut();
83:             let mut guest = borrow.producer();
84:             guest.begin_frame();
85: 
86:             let (root, next_id) = {
87:                 let mut walk = Walk {
88:                     guest: &mut guest,
89:                     next_id: self.next_id,
90:                     reactive: &mut reactive,
91:                 };
92:                 let root = walk.any(AnyView::new(view), env, ROOT_PARENT)?;
93:                 (root, walk.next_id)
94:             };

96:             guest.end_frame();
97:             (root, next_id)
98:         };
99:         self.next_id = next_id;
100: 
101:         for binding in reactive {
102:             let transport = Rc::clone(&self.transport);
103:             match binding {
104:                 Reactive::Text { node, content } => {
105:                     let guard = content.watch(move |ctx| {
106:                         let text = ctx.into_value().to_plain().to_string();
107:                         let mut borrow = transport.borrow_mut();
108:                         let mut guest = borrow.producer();
109:                         guest.begin_frame();
110:                         let _ = guest.set_text(node, &text);
111:                         guest.end_frame();
112:                     });

145:         id
146:     }
147: 
148:     fn insert(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
149:         if parent != ROOT_PARENT {
150:             self.guest.insert_child(parent, child, pathland_core::APPEND)?;
151:         }
152:         Ok(())
153:     }
154: 
155:     fn any(&mut self, view: AnyView, env: &Environment, parent: u32) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
156:         // `Metadata<Environment>` carries a scoped environment (WaterUI injects
157:         // the stack `Axis` this way); recurse into the content with that env.
158:         if view.is::<Metadata<Environment>>() {
159:             let m = *view.downcast::<Metadata<Environment>>().expect("downcast environment");
160:             return self.any(m.content, &m.value, parent);
161:         }
162:         // `Metadata<Retain>` keeps watcher guards alive for the subtree's
163:         // lifetime; unwrap it (the retained value is dropped, which for a
164:         // static tree holds no guards).
165:         if view.is::<Metadata<Retain>>() {
166:             let m = *view.downcast::<Metadata<Retain>>().expect("downcast retain");
167:             return self.any(m.content, env, parent);
168:         }
169:         if view.is::<Native<FixedContainer>>() {
170:             let c = *view
171:                 .downcast::<Native<FixedContainer>>()
172:                 .expect("downcast container");
173:             return self.container(c, env, parent);
174:         }
175:         if view.is::<Native<TextConfig>>() {
176:             let c = *view.downcast::<Native<TextConfig>>().expect("downcast text");
177:             return self.text_node(c, parent);
178:         }
179:         if view.is::<Native<ButtonConfig>>() {
180:             let c = *view.downcast::<Native<ButtonConfig>>().expect("downcast button");
181:             return self.button_node(c, parent);
182:         }
183:         if view.is::<Native<Spacer>>() {
184:             let _s = *view.downcast::<Native<Spacer>>().expect("downcast spacer");
185:             return self.spacer_node(parent);
186:         }
187: 
188:         // Composite view: expand its body and keep walking.
189:         let body = view.body(env);
190:         self.any(AnyView::new(body), env, parent)
191:     }
192: 
193:     fn container(
194:         &mut self,
195:         container: Native<FixedContainer>,
196:         env: &Environment,
197:         parent: u32,
198:     ) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
199:         let inner = container.into_inner();
200:         let stack_axis = inner.stack_axis();
201:         let (_layout, contents) = inner.into_inner();
202: 
203:         let (ct, spacing) = match stack_axis {
204:             Some(LazyStackAxis::Vertical { spacing, .. }) => (component_type::VSTACK, Some(spacing)),
205:             Some(LazyStackAxis::Horizontal { spacing, .. }) => {
206:                 (component_type::HSTACK, Some(spacing))
207:             }
208:             None => {
209:                 let axis = env.get::<Axis>().copied().unwrap_or(Axis::Vertical);
210:                 let ct = if axis.is_horizontal() {
211:                     component_type::HSTACK
212:                 } else {
213:                     component_type::VSTACK
214:                 };
215:                 (ct, None)
216:             }
217:         };
218: 
219:         let id = self.alloc_id();
220:         self.guest.create_node(id, ct)?;
221:         self.insert(parent, id)?;
222:         if let Some(spacing) = spacing {
223:             self.guest.set_property(
224:                 id,
225:                 property_id::SPACING,
226:                 value_type::F32,
227:                 spacing.get().to_bits(),
228:             )?;
229:             self.reactive.push(Reactive::Property {
230:                 node: id,
231:                 property: property_id::SPACING,
232:                 value: spacing,
233:             });
234:         }
235: 
236:         for child in contents {
237:             self.any(child, env, id)?;
238:         }
239:         Ok(id)
240:     }
241: 
242:     fn text_node(&mut self, config: Native<TextConfig>, parent: u32) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
243:         let config = config.into_inner();
244:         self.emit_leaf(component_type::TEXT, config.content, parent)
245:     }
246: 
247:     fn button_node(&mut self, config: Native<ButtonConfig>, parent: u32) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
248:         let config = config.into_inner();
249:         // `ButtonConfig` is produced by `Button::body(env)`, which resolves the
250:         // label and stores the resolved content as the accessibility label.
251:         let content = config.label.accessibility_label();
252:         self.emit_leaf(component_type::BUTTON, content, parent)
253:     }
254: 
255:     fn emit_leaf(
256:         &mut self,
257:         ct: u16,
258:         content: Computed<StyledStr>,
259:         parent: u32,
260:     ) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
261:         let text = content.get().to_plain().to_string();
262: 
263:         let id = self.alloc_id();
264:         self.guest.create_node(id, ct)?;
265:         self.insert(parent, id)?;
266:         self.guest.set_text(id, &text)?;
267: 
268:         self.reactive.push(Reactive::Text { node: id, content });
269:         Ok(id)
270:     }
271: 
272:     fn spacer_node(&mut self, parent: u32) -> Result<u32, RingError> {

274:         self.guest.create_node(id, component_type::SPACER)?;
275:         self.insert(parent, id)?;

1: //! Bump arena for variable-length data in linear memory.
2: //!
3: //! Every entry is self-describing: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`. Opcodes
4: //! reference entries by their byte offset (`arenaRef`), so the entry length is
5: //! read directly from the arena and every opcode stays 16 bytes.
6: 
7: use crate::memory::header;
8: 
9: /// Errors produced by the arena.
10: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
11: pub enum ArenaError {
12:     /// Not enough remaining bytes for the allocation.
13:     OutOfSpace,
14:     /// The arena offset is out of bounds or points to an invalid entry.
15:     InvalidOffset,
16: }
17: 
18: /// Allocate `bytes` into the arena region, returning its byte offset.
19: ///
20: /// The cursor lives in the header block (`OFF_ARENA_CURSOR`).
21: #[inline]
22: pub(crate) fn alloc(data: &mut [u8], header: &mut [u8], bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
23:     let cursor = header::get_u32(header, crate::memory::OFF_ARENA_CURSOR) as usize;
24:     let len = bytes.len();
25:     let needed = 4 + len;
26:     if cursor + needed > data.len() {
27:         return Err(ArenaError::OutOfSpace);
28:     }
29:     data[cursor..cursor + 4].copy_from_slice(&(len as u32).to_le_bytes());
30:     data[cursor + 4..cursor + needed].copy_from_slice(bytes);
31:     header::set_u32(header, crate::memory::OFF_ARENA_CURSOR, (cursor + needed) as u32);
32:     Ok(cursor as u32)
33: }
34: 
35: /// Allocate a string, returning its arena offset.
36: #[inline]
37: pub(crate) fn alloc_str(
38:     data: &mut [u8],
39:     header: &mut [u8],
40:     s: &str,
41: ) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
42:     alloc(data, header, s.as_bytes())
43: }
44: 
45: /// Read the bytes of the entry at `offset` from an arena region.
46: #[inline]
47: pub(crate) fn get(data: &[u8], offset: u32) -> Result<&[u8], ArenaError> {
48:     let off = offset as usize;
49:     if off + 4 > data.len() {
50:         return Err(ArenaError::InvalidOffset);
51:     }
52:     let len = u32::from_le_bytes(data[off..off + 4].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
53:     if off + 4 + len > data.len() {
54:         return Err(ArenaError::InvalidOffset);
55:     }
56:     Ok(&data[off + 4..off + 4 + len])
57: }
58: 
59: /// Read the string at `offset` (UTF-8 validated).
60: #[inline]
