## Command Tables

### TREE (0x01)

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — | Create a node of `componentType` |
| `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — | Delete a node and its subtree |
| `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | `0x0001` = append | Insert `childId` into `parentId` at `index` |
| `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — | Remove `childId` from `parentId` |
| `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | `0x0001` = append | Move child to `newIndex` (after removal) |

### STYLE (0x02)

The engine does not emit positions. `STYLE` carries the **constraint properties**
that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, alignment, FILL/HUG
size hints — plus **styling modifiers** (padding, colors, fonts, borders).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
| `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
| `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |

`SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:

```
B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
```

#### Value types

| Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
|------------|-------|--------------------|
| `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
| `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
| `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
| `F32` | `0x04` | f32 |
| `STRING` | `0x05` | arenaRef (utf8) |
| `ENUM` | `0x06` | low byte of C |
| `COLOR` | `0x07` | packed `0xAARRGGBB` |
| `DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x08` | arenaRef (token path) |

#### Constraint properties for native layout

The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
native equivalents (e.g. `SPACING` → GTK box spacing / CSS `gap`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`
→ size requests). Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL (expand to
available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT (native intrinsic size).

| Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
|----------|-------|------|----------------|
| `SPACING` | `0x0001` | F32 | Gap between children |
| `ALIGNMENT` | `0x0002` | ENUM | Cross-axis alignment |
| `WIDTH` | `0x100B` | F32 | Width hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
| `HEIGHT` | `0x100C` | F32 | Height hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |

#### Styling properties (modifiers)

Styling properties are **modifiers** — they apply to any view, not just stacks —
and map to visual decoration rather than layout. `PADDING` (uniform) and its
per-edge variants map to widget margins / CSS `padding`, alongside
`COLOR`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`/`BORDER_*`:

| Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |

### EVENT (0x03) — host → guest

Events are the **raw inputs**: the renderer reports what happened (a pointer
went down/moved/up, a key went down/up) and resolves which node it hit via its
own rendered-output tree. High-level interpretations — tap, drag, long-press —
are built by the guest/app from these raw inputs and are **not** part of the
protocol.

#### Event listeners (which nodes emit events)

A renderer reports raw events only for nodes that declared they want them. The
application declares this intent through the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic
property (`0x2005`, a u32 bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type).
Each bit requests a raw-input event kind (see [`listener`] flags):

| Bit | Mask | Event command | Meaning |
|-----|------|---------------|---------|
| 0 | `0x00000001` | `POINTER_DOWN` | Report pointer-down for this node |
| 1 | `0x00000002` | `POINTER_MOVE` | Report pointer-move/enter/leave |
| 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` | Report pointer-up for this node |
| 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` | Report key-down |
| 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` | Report key-up |

This is what makes **any element** (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit
events — the renderer attaches native input recognition to the matching native
element when the listener bit is set, not only to buttons. A renderer SHOULD
report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP` for a node with the `POINTER_DOWN`/
`POINTER_UP` bits set by attaching a native click/press gesture to that
element.

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `POINTER_DOWN` | `0x01` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` | Pointer button pressed at viewport-relative point |
| `POINTER_MOVE` | `0x02` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` / `HOVER_LEAVE` | Pointer moved (bit 0 = entered/hovering, bit 1 = leaving) |
| `POINTER_UP` | `0x03` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` | Pointer button released at viewport-relative point |
| `KEY_DOWN` | `0x04` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` | Key pressed (bit 1 = auto-repeat) |
| `KEY_UP` | `0x05` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | Key released |

### Payload encoding conventions

- **Float payloads** (`spacing`, `padding`, sizes) are stored as raw `f32` (IEEE 754) bit patterns in a `u32` field.
- **Node IDs** are `u32`.
- **Component types / property IDs** are `u16`; when packed into a 4-byte payload they occupy the low two bytes (the high bytes are reserved / zero unless documented).
- **Arena references** are a `u32` byte offset into the arena region (see [Arena](#arena)).
- **Colors** are packed `0xAARRGGBB` in sRGB (see [Colors](#colors)).

### Reserved ranges

- `Category == 0` is reserved (invalid).
- `Command == 0` in any category is reserved (invalid).
- `Category 0x80-0xFF`: custom/extended categories.

| Category | Value | Name | Producer | Description |

| `TREE` | `0x01` | Tree mutations | Guest engine | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
| `STYLE` | `0x02` | Constraints & tokens | Guest engine | Property values (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
| `EVENT` | `0x03` | Raw inputs | Host renderer | Pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
| `META` | `0x04` | Control | Both | Reset, environment |

1: //! # pathland-render-html
2: //!
3: //! A Pathland renderer that maps opcode frames onto **declarative HTML**
4: //! elements. Like every Pathland renderer it is a pure function of the opcode
5: //! stream: it retains only its own decoded output tree (a cache), never
6: //! application state, and emits `WHAT` the UI is — never layout rects. Native
7: //! browser layout does the positioning.
8: //!
9: //! This is the "server-side render" / remote-projection target (Goal #15): the
10: //! same opcode stream that drives a native backend drives this HTML document.
11: //!
12: //! Frames are **self-contained**: `apply(opcodes, strings)` resolves `SET_TEXT`
13: //! by a *relative* offset into the frame's own string section (no mirrored
14: //! arena), and every rendered element carries a stable `data-pathland-id` so a
15: //! client can hydrate it and apply later deltas in place.
16: 
17: use std::collections::BTreeMap;

content.text: Toggle support is complete and verified end-to-end. **What changed** - **Protocol** (`constants.rs` + `spec/OPCODE.md`): added `component_type::CHECKBOX = 0x000D`; `value_type_for` now returns `U8` for `SELECTED`; documented `SELECTED` (0/1 checked state) + `CHECKBOX`. - **Producer** (`producer.rs`): `toggle_node` maps `ToggleStyle::Checkbox → CHECKBOX`, `Automatic`/`Switch → SWITCH` (non-exhaustive `_` → SWITCH), emits the label via `SET_TEXT` (reactive), the checked state via `SELECTED` (reactive `Computed`), and registers a flip closure (`t.set(!t.get())`) in the existing action map — so `invoke`/`PointerUp` works unchanged. - **Consumer** (`consumer.rs`): rebuilds `SWITCH`/`CHECKBOX` → `Toggle` (fresh `Binding` seeded from `SELECTED`, `.switch()`/`.checkbox()`), keeping the lossless round-trip green. - **Renderer** (`render-html`): renders both as ``, plus pill CSS for switches. - **Web demo** (`app.js` + `main.rs`): `applyBatch` now handles `SET_PROPERTY(SELECTED)` and routes toggle-label `SET_TEXT` to the inner span; a `change` listener sends `PointerUp`; demo shows a switch ("Notifications") + a checkbox ("Checkbox"). **Verification** - `pathland-waterui`: 13/13 tests (incl. `toggle_round_trips`, `reactive_toggle_emits_delta`, `toggle_action_flips_binding`). - `lib/rust` full suite green; `render-html` 5/5. - Web demo builds clean; live SSR shows `` (Notifications) and `` (Checkbox). Note: the demo `counter_view` now takes a second `Binding` parameter — adjust any other call sites if you later share it.

2: //!
3: //! Events are the **raw inputs** the renderer reports: pointer down/move/up and
4: //! key down/up, each carrying a host-resolved `targetId`. High-level
5: //! interpretations (tap, drag, long-press) are built by the guest/app from
6: //! these raw inputs and are NOT part of the protocol.

8: //! Encode a raw input with `Event::encode`, decode a ring opcode with
9: //! `Event::try_from`.

128: /// Build a pointer-opcode flags word from the pointer/hover bits.
129: #[inline]
130: fn flag_for(secondary: bool, hovering: bool, leaving: bool) -> u16 {
131:     let mut flags = 0u16;
132:     if secondary {
133:         flags |= flag::POINTER_SECONDARY;
134:     }
135:     if hovering {
136:         flags |= flag::HOVER_ENTER;
137:     }
138:     if leaving {
139:         flags |= flag::HOVER_LEAVE;
140:     }
141:     flags
142: }

144: /// Error decoding a raw-input event from an opcode.
145: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
146: pub enum EventError {
147:     /// The opcode is not an `EVENT` category opcode.
148:     NotAnEvent,
149:     /// The opcode is an EVENT category opcode but an unknown command.
150:     UnknownCommand,
151: }

153: impl TryFrom<Opcode> for Event {
154:     type Error = EventError;

156:     fn try_from(op: Opcode) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
157:         if op.category() != category::EVENT {

162:             crate::event::POINTER_DOWN => Ok(Event::PointerDown {

178:                 y: op.c_f32(),
179:                 secondary: flags & flag::POINTER_SECONDARY != 0,
180:             }),
181:             crate::event::KEY_DOWN => Ok(Event::KeyDown {
182:                 target: op.a(),
183:                 key_code: op.b() as u16,
184:                 modifiers: op.c() as u8,

content.text: ## Recommendation: **Slider** is the next natural component It continues the control progression you've already started — **Button** (action) → **Toggle** (boolean binding) → **Slider** (numeric binding) — and maps cleanly onto a real native primitive (``). It also introduces the one protocol concept the remaining controls all need (a *value-bearing* event), making it the right architectural stepping stone before TextField/Stepper. **Why not the alternatives:** - **TextField** — text editing brings focus/cursor/IME/submit semantics; explicitly deferred in `AGENTS.md` ("TEXT_FIELD editing"). Reuses the same value-event idea later, so Slider de-risks it. - **ScrollView** — a container, not a control; no value events (simpler, but a different shape than the control family). - **Image** — needs binary asset transport (bigger lift). ## The one new concept this needs Toggle could reuse `POINTER_UP` + an app-side flip because the state is just `!bool`. A slider's value is continuous — the renderer (which owns geometry) must resolve the pointer position to a numeric value and report it back. So this plan adds a **`VALUE_CHANGED` event** (host → guest), mirroring how the renderer already resolves a raw pointer to a `targetId`. ## Plan (Slider) **1. Protocol — `pathland-core` + `spec/OPCODE.md`** - `component_type::SLIDER = 0x000E`. - Properties: `VALUE = 0x2006` (F32), `MIN_VALUE = 0x2007` (F32), `MAX_VALUE = 0x2008` (F32); `value_type_for` maps them to `F32` (already the default). - New `event::VALUE_CHANGED = 0x06`; `Event::ValueChanged { target: u32, value: f32 }` with `A=targetId, B=value.to_bits()` in `events.rs` (encode + `TryFrom`) — flows through `decode_events` automatically. **2. Producer — `pathland-waterui/src/producer.rs`** - Handle `Native` → `slider_node`: - `create_node(SLIDER)` + label via `emit_leaf` path (reactive text). - Emit `MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE` from `config.range` (f64 → f32 bits), and `VALUE` from `config.value`. - Push `Reactive::Property` over `config.value.map(|v| (v as f32).to_bits())` for live re-emit. - Register the `Binding` in a new `values: BTreeMap>` (mirrors `actions`). - New `Emitter::set_value(node_id, value, env)` that clamps to the stored range and calls `binding.set(...)`. **3. Consumer — `consumer.rs`** - `rebuild` maps `SLIDER` → `Slider::new(label, &binding(value)).range(min..=max)`. **4. Renderer — `pathland-render-html`** - `SLIDER` → ``. **5. Web client + demo** - `app.js`: handle `SET_PROPERTY(VALUE)` (set `input.value`); add an `input`/`change` listener on `input[type=range]` that sends a `VALUE_CHANGED` opcode (encode target + value). - `main.rs`: `Binding` + a `slider("Volume", &volume)` in `counter_view`; the server maps `Event::ValueChanged` → `emitter.set_value(...)`. **6. Tests** - `roundtrip.rs`: `slider_round_trips`, `reactive_slider_emits_delta`, `slider_set_value_clamps`. - `events.rs`: `ValueChanged` round-trip + conformance vector. - `render-html`: `renders_slider` (assert `min`/`max`/`value`). ## Please confirm before I proceed 1. **Component** — Slider (recommended), or would you prefer TextField/ScrollView next? 2. **Value event** — OK to extend the `EVENT` category with a semantic `VALUE_CHANGED` (renderer resolves value, like it resolves `targetId`)? This is the biggest protocol decision. 3. **Range/encoding** — two `F32` properties (`MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE`) + `VALUE` (f64→f32), fine? 4. **Live vs commit updates** — send `VALUE_CHANGED` continuously on `input` (recommended, real-time) or only on `change` (release)?

content.text: Committed as `c3a63b4` with a clean working tree.
There is an issue causing server time ticks to emit 2 events. One is the new text for "Count: <number>". The other is a smaller event I cannot decipher.

## Diagnosis: the second event is the reactive `BORDER_COLOR` delta

Each timer tick does `count.set(count.get() + 1)`, and `count` drives **two** reactive bindings in `counter_view`:

1. `label = count.map(|c| format!("Count: {c}")).computed()` → the `SET_TEXT` you recognize.
2. `border = signal_color(count.map(|c| if c % 2 == 0 { Color::red() } else { Color::blue() }).computed())` → the producer's `border_props` (`pathland-waterui/src/producer.rs`) subscribes a `Reactive::Property` on the packed border color, so every tick flips red↔blue and emits a **`SET_PROPERTY(BORDER_COLOR)`** delta.

It's "smaller" because it's a single 16-byte opcode with an **empty string section** (vs `SET_TEXT`, which carries the string payload).

**Why it looks like a bug:** `app.js` only applies `SET_TEXT`, `SET_PROPERTY(SELECTED)`, and `SET_PROPERTY(VALUE)` — it **ignores `BORDER_COLOR`**. So the browser receives the delta but the border never visibly changes, making it look like a spurious/no-op event. The behavior is correct per the reactive-border feature we built; it's just invisible in the live browser.

## Options

**A — Make the live border actually update** (recommended if you want the reactive border to be real)
- Teach `app.js` to handle `SET_PROPERTY(BORDER_COLOR)` (packed `0xAARRGGBB` → `rgba(...)`), set per-edge `borderTopColor`/`borderRightColor`/`borderBottomColor`/`borderLeftColor` on the bordered element.
- Result: 2 events/tick remain, but both are meaningful — the border visibly flips red↔blue with the count.

**B — Make the demo border static** (if you want 1 event/tick)
- Replace `signal_color(...)` with a plain `Color::red()` (or another static color). Each tick then emits only the count `SET_TEXT`. The border no longer reacts to parity.

**C — Leave as-is** (it's working as designed).

Which do you want — A (make the reactive border visible in the browser), B (static border, single event), or C?

# pathland-waterui

The Pathland backend for [WaterUI](https://github.com/water-rs/waterui): a bridge
that makes WaterUI the application layer and Pathland the protocol layer.

Pathland is **web-only**: native (Apple/GTK) renders through WaterUI directly.
This crate is the producer side of that split — a server serializes a WaterUI
view tree into Pathland opcodes, projects them to a browser (SSR → HTML, then
live deltas + events over WebSocket), and routes input events back into the
application.

## What it does

Two sides of the same protocol, in one crate:

| Module | Direction | Purpose |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `producer` (`Emitter`) | WaterUI view → Pathland opcodes | Walk a view tree and emit the declarative structure as self-contained frames |
| `consumer` (`Consumer`) | Pathland opcodes → retained description | Decode frames into a retained node map; `rebuild()` reconstructs WaterUI views (lossless round-trip checks) |

Neither side knows the other's private machinery — WaterUI owns change
detection and native rendering, Pathland owns the 16-byte opcode wire format
(see `spec/OPCODE.md`).

## Mapped components

The producer walks the view tree, expanding composite views through
`View::body` and mapping the native leaves it recognizes:

| WaterUI | Pathland component |
|---------|--------------------|
| `VStack` / `HStack` | `VSTACK` / `HSTACK` |
| `Text` | `TEXT` |
| `Button` | `BUTTON` |
| `Spacer` | `SPACER` |
| `Toggle` (switch / checkbox style) | `SWITCH` / `CHECKBOX` |
| `Slider` | `SLIDER` |
| `.border(...)` modifier | `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_COLOR` / `BORDER_RADIUS` / `BORDER_EDGES` |

Unrecognized native leaves are the ones Pathland does not model yet — they
fail loudly rather than silently degrade (see `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full
component catalog).

## Reactive emission

WaterUI writable signals live in the engine. While walking, the producer
subscribes to the reactive fields it cares about:

- text content (`SET_TEXT`)
- properties such as stack `SPACING`, `BORDER_COLOR`, toggle `SELECTED`, and
  slider `VALUE` (`SET_PROPERTY`)

A later `set()` on a bound signal re-emits **only** the affected node as a
delta frame — no full tree walk.

## Frames are self-contained

Each frame is pushed to the sink as `(opcodes, strings)`. `SET_TEXT` references
its string by a **relative** offset into that frame's own string section, so a
consumer needs no ring, no mirrored arena, and no prior state to decode a
frame. Nothing is aggregated and nothing is sent on connect — the browser
hydrates the initial SSR HTML and applies each delta in place.

## Interaction

Button actions and toggle flips are captured into a `nodeId → action` map;
slider values into a `nodeId → Binding<f64>` map. A host dispatches inbound
events back into the app:

- `Emitter::invoke(node_id, env)` — button `POINTER_UP`, toggle flip
- `Emitter::set_value(node_id, value)` — slider `VALUE_CHANGED`

## Usage

```rust
use pathland_waterui::Emitter;

let mut emitter = Emitter::with_sink(|opcodes, strings| {
    // encode_frame(&opcodes, &strings) -> WebSocket batch
});
let root = emitter.emit(my_view, &env);
// ... on input: emitter.invoke(target, &env) / emitter.set_value(target, v)
```

## Building

The `waterui` umbrella dependency pulls `waterkit-build`, which compiles Swift,
so a clean build needs the Xcode toolchain on the path:

```sh
export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
export SDKROOT=$(xcrun --sdk macosx --show-sdk-path)
export PATH="/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/bin:$PATH"
```

## Testing

```sh
cd pathland-waterui && cargo test
```

Runs the producer → consumer round-trips (structure, reactive deltas, action
and value dispatch) in `tests/roundtrip.rs`.

content.text:
The consumer side uses **retained** in the retained-mode sense: it keeps an id-keyed map of the *decoded declarative structure* as a cache of its own output, so it can be inspected incrementally and rebuilt back into WaterUI views.

## The retained data model

`Consumer` holds `nodes: BTreeMap<u32, Node>` (`consumer.rs:65`). Each `Node` (`consumer.rs:33`) is the wire structure, not platform widgets:

```rust
pub struct Node {
    component: u16,          // protocol component type id (VSTACK, TEXT, SWITCH, …)
    text: Option<String>,    // SET_TEXT content
    properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>, // propertyId → raw wire value (bits)
    children: Vec<u32>,      // child node ids, in insertion order
}
```

This is exactly what the README calls the **"retained node description"** — a mirror of `pathland-render-gtk`'s `RenderTree`, but with no native element attached. Per Pathland's statelessness principle (renderer statelessness), it's a *cache of the renderer's own output*, never application state.

## How the retained map is built and mutated

`apply(opcodes, strings)` (`consumer.rs:77`) mutates the retained map incrementally, frame by frame:

- **TREE** opcodes edit structure: `CREATE_NODE` inserts a node, `DELETE_NODE` removes it, `INSERT_CHILD`/`REMOVE_CHILD`/`MOVE_CHILD` edit `children`.
- **STYLE** opcodes edit contents: `SET_TEXT` sets `node.text` (resolved by relative offset into the self-contained frame's string section), `SET_PROPERTY` inserts into `node.properties`.

Because deltas arrive as self-contained frames, a later `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` delta simply updates the existing retained node in place — nothing is aggregated and no prior state is needed.

## How it's read back

- `node(id)` — read a single retained node.
- `rebuild(id)` (`consumer.rs:152`) — walks the retained tree and reconstructs **WaterUI views** from it: `VStack`/`HStack` (with spacing), `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`, `Toggle` (switch/checkbox), and `Slider` (with range). For controls it seeds a fresh `Binding` from the retained wire values (`SELECTED` → toggle state, `VALUE`/`MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE` → slider), so re-emitting reproduces the same structure.

## Where it's used

The consumer is test-only (per `AGENTS.md`): `tests/roundtrip.rs` drives `emit → apply → rebuild → re-emit` and asserts the two `Consumer` trees are equal (`rebuild_is_lossless`), proving the protocol survives a full round trip. The retained map is what makes that comparison possible — it's the stable, id-keyed description both the producer and the consumer agree on.
But is it strcitly required to have a reteined model in the consumer? Why so?

Not strictly for a *single* frame — but it **is** required for the consumer's actual job, because the protocol is **delta-based**.

## When retention is not needed

A decoder that only ever receives one complete, self-contained frame (the initial render: all `CREATE_NODE` + `INSERT_CHILD` + `SET_TEXT` + `SET_PROPERTY` ops) could build the description in one pass and discard the opcodes — no retained map. `rebuild_is_lossless` alone would work that way.

## Why the consumer actually needs it

The round-trip tests don't stop at one frame. The reactive tests do:

```
emit view          → apply initial frame (builds the tree)
binding.set(...)   → apply delta frame (only SET_TEXT/SET_PROPERTY for one node)
assert node text   → read the accumulated structure
```

A delta frame is **not self-sufficient**: `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`INSERT_CHILD` reference existing nodes **by id** and carry only the change. Without the prior structure you cannot:
- know what `node 3` is to apply `SET_TEXT` to it, or
- rebuild the full tree, since the tree is spread across the initial frame + every delta that followed.

So retention is required for the consumer's two purposes:

1. **Applying delta frames incrementally** — deltas mutate an existing tree, so the previous structure must be kept.
2. **The lossless comparison** (`consumer == consumer2`) — it compares the *whole accumulated* retained tree, which only exists if you retained across frames.

## Why this isn't a violation of renderer statelessness

The retained map is the renderer's **output tree** — a cache of what the opcode stream decoded — never application state. The application owns the canonical WaterUI tree; the consumer only caches its own decode. This is exactly the same pattern the real renderers use (`HtmlRenderer` keeps `BTreeMap<u32, Node>`, `pathland-render-gtk` keeps `id → widget`): to apply deltas, any renderer must retain its output. The consumer just keeps the *declarative description* instead of platform widgets.

## The alternative, and why it falls short

A stateless consumer (decode one full frame → view, discard) would be simpler but could **not** validate the reactive delta path — which is the headline feature the round-trip suite exists to prove. So for a test-only consumer, retention is the minimal design that exercises the real protocol semantics.

If you'd like, I can add a short "Why the consumer is retained" note to the README to make this reasoning explicit.
But it is expected that the rendering backend has a tree, fx a DOM

Exactly — that's the key point, and it's why the consumer's retained map isn't a special burden. A rendering backend is **expected** to keep an output tree; that's the standard retained-mode contract for a delta-driven protocol.

## The DOM analogy

When you apply incremental updates to a DOM, the browser doesn't re-derive the whole page from scratch each time — it mutates the tree it already holds, because each update references existing nodes by id ("set text on node 3", "insert node 7 under node 2"). The DOM *is* the retained model; it exists precisely so deltas can be applied in place.

Pathland's real renderers follow the same contract:
- `HtmlRenderer` keeps `BTreeMap<u32, Node>` (`render-html`) so it can re-render SSR HTML after each delta frame.
- `pathland-render-gtk` keeps `id → gtk::Widget`.
- The browser's DOM is the client-side tree for the web path.

## What the consumer is

The consumer (`pathland-waterui`) is that same pattern in miniature: it plays the renderer's role — "apply deltas to a retained tree" — but holds a **declarative description** (`component`, `text`, `properties`, `children`) instead of DOM nodes or widgets, because it renders nothing. Its `Node` is deliberately the *same shape* as `render-html`'s `Node`, so the round-trip tests validate against the structure a real renderer would keep.

So the answer to "is retention strictly required?" resolves cleanly: **retention is required because delta application is required, and a retained output tree is the mechanism every renderer uses for that** — the DOM is the canonical proof. The consumer just demonstrates it in the simplest form, with a description tree instead of native elements.

The one distinction worth keeping explicit: the consumer is *test-only* and holds no widgets, so unlike a real renderer it never draws or hit-tests — but its retained-map contract is identical.

Confirmed. No — the demo does not use the `Consumer` at all.

The web demo (`examples/pathland-web/src/main.rs`) imports:
- `pathland_waterui::Emitter` (produces frames)
- `pathland_render_html::HtmlRenderer` (renders SSR HTML + keeps its **own** `BTreeMap<u32, Node>` retained tree)
- `pathland_core_transport::{encode_frame, decode_events}`

`pathland_waterui::Consumer` is used **only** in `pathland-waterui/tests/roundtrip.rs` (the round-trip tests), plus its export in `src/lib.rs`. It is test-only, as `AGENTS.md` states.

So there are actually **two** retained node trees in the picture, and they serve different purposes:
- `render-html`'s `HtmlRenderer.nodes` — the *real* server-side renderer tree, used by the demo to apply deltas and re-render SSR HTML.
- `pathland-waterui`'s `Consumer.nodes` — the *test-only* mirror, used to validate lossless round-trips, never exercised by the demo.

Okay..  That should really be much more clear.. If the consumer is only for tests - and is neded for test going forward - then is should be named as such and the readme.md should clearly state that it is only there for tests. If is not needed for tests either, the we should be able just just remove it

## Determination: the consumer **is** needed for the round-trip tests

Grep confirms `Consumer` is used only by `tests/roundtrip.rs` (never by the demo or any other crate). And it provides two things the tests genuinely rely on:

1. **A retained decoder to apply delta frames** — the reactive tests (`reactive_text_emits_delta`, `reactive_toggle_emits_delta`, `reactive_slider_emits_delta`, …) apply the initial frame *and then* a delta frame, then assert on the **accumulated** state. That requires a retained tree.
2. **`rebuild()`** — the only way to reconstruct WaterUI views from the wire. It powers `rebuild_is_lossless` (emit → decode → rebuild → re-emit → `assert_eq!(consumer, consumer2)`), which is the "the protocol survives a full WaterUI round trip" guarantee.

So it can't just be removed without dropping real test coverage. The fix is to label it unambiguously as test-only.

## Proposed plan

**Option A (recommended) — move it out of the library API into the test suite**
- New `pathland-waterui/tests/support/` holding the decoder (rename to `RoundTripDecoder`, or keep `Consumer`); `tests/roundtrip.rs` imports it via `mod support;`.
- `src/lib.rs`: remove `pub mod consumer;` / `pub use consumer::Consumer;` — the crate's public surface becomes producer-only (`Emitter`).
- Update `Cargo.toml` description + `lib.rs` module docs accordingly.

**Option B (lighter) — keep it in the library but rename + document**
- Rename `Consumer` → `TestConsumer` (or `RoundTripConsumer`), keep it public but add a doc comment: *test support only; the runtime backend is the producer (`Emitter`)*.

**README updates (both options)**
- Rewrite the consumer row: runtime surface = the producer; the round-trip decoder is **test-only**, living in the test suite, used solely by `tests/roundtrip.rs` (delta application + `rebuild` for the lossless round-trip).
- Add a short "why a retained decoder" note tying back to the retained-output-tree / DOM framing we discussed, so the test-only retained model isn't mistaken for the runtime renderer tree.

## Two questions before I execute

1. **Which option** — A (move to `tests/support/`, remove from library API) or B (rename in-library + docs)?
2. **Name** — `RoundTripDecoder`, `TestConsumer`, or keep `Consumer`?
1: A. 2: TestConsumer

1: # pathland-waterui
2: 
3: The Pathland backend for [WaterUI](https://github.com/water-rs/waterui): a bridge
4: that makes WaterUI the application layer and Pathland the protocol layer.
5: 
6: Pathland is **web-only**: native (Apple/GTK) renders through WaterUI directly.
7: This crate is the producer side of that split — a server serializes a WaterUI
8: view tree into Pathland opcodes, projects them to a browser (SSR → HTML, then
9: live deltas + events over WebSocket), and routes input events back into the
10: application.
11: 
12: ## What it does
13: 
14: Two sides of the same protocol, in one crate:
15: 
16: | Module | Direction | Purpose |
17: |--------|-----------|---------|
18: | `producer` (`Emitter`) | WaterUI view → Pathland opcodes | Walk a view tree and emit the declarative structure as self-contained frames |
19: | `consumer` (`Consumer`) | Pathland opcodes → retained description | Decode frames into a retained node map; `rebuild()` reconstructs WaterUI views (lossless round-trip checks) |
20: 
21: Neither side knows the other's private machinery — WaterUI owns change
22: detection and native rendering, Pathland owns the 16-byte opcode wire format
23: (see `spec/OPCODE.md`).
24: 
25: ## Mapped components
26: 
27: The producer walks the view tree, expanding composite views through
28: `View::body` and mapping the native leaves it recognizes:
29: 
30: | WaterUI | Pathland component |
31: |---------|--------------------|
32: | `VStack` / `HStack` | `VSTACK` / `HSTACK` |
33: | `Text` | `TEXT` |
34: | `Button` | `BUTTON` |
35: | `Spacer` | `SPACER` |
36: | `Toggle` (switch / checkbox style) | `SWITCH` / `CHECKBOX` |
37: | `Slider` | `SLIDER` |
38: | `.border(...)` modifier | `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_COLOR` / `BORDER_RADIUS` / `BORDER_EDGES` |
39: 
40: Unrecognized native leaves are the ones Pathland does not model yet — they
41: fail loudly rather than silently degrade (see `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full
42: component catalog).
43: 
44: ## Reactive emission
45: 
46: WaterUI writable signals live in the engine. While walking, the producer
47: subscribes to the reactive fields it cares about:
48: 
49: - text content (`SET_TEXT`)
50: - properties such as stack `SPACING`, `BORDER_COLOR`, toggle `SELECTED`, and
51:   slider `VALUE` (`SET_PROPERTY`)
52: 
53: A later `set()` on a bound signal re-emits **only** the affected node as a
54: delta frame — no full tree walk.
55: 
56: ## Frames are self-contained
57: 
58: Each frame is pushed to the sink as `(opcodes, strings)`. `SET_TEXT` references
59: its string by a **relative** offset into that frame's own string section, so a
60: consumer needs no ring, no mirrored arena, and no prior state to decode a
61: frame. Nothing is aggregated and nothing is sent on connect — the browser
62: hydrates the initial SSR HTML and applies each delta in place.
63: 
64: ## Interaction
65: 
66: Button actions and toggle flips are captured into a `nodeId → action` map;
67: slider values into a `nodeId → Binding<f64>` map. A host dispatches inbound
68: events back into the app:
69: 
70: - `Emitter::invoke(node_id, env)` — button `POINTER_UP`, toggle flip
71: - `Emitter::set_value(node_id, value)` — slider `VALUE_CHANGED`
72: 
73: ## Usage
74: 
75: ```rust
76: use pathland_waterui::Emitter;
77: 
78: let mut emitter = Emitter::with_sink(|opcodes, strings| {
79:     // encode_frame(&opcodes, &strings) -> WebSocket batch
80: });
81: let root = emitter.emit(my_view, &env);
82: // ... on input: emitter.invoke(target, &env) / emitter.set_value(target, v)
83: ```
84: 
85: ## Building
86: 
87: The `waterui` umbrella dependency pulls `waterkit-build`, which compiles Swift,
88: so a clean build needs the Xcode toolchain on the path:
89: 
90: ```sh
91: export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
92: export SDKROOT=$(xcrun --sdk macosx --show-sdk-path)
93: export PATH="/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/bin:$PATH"
94: ```
95: 
96: ## Testing
97: 
98: ```sh
99: cd pathland-waterui && cargo test
100: ```
101: 
102: Runs the producer → consumer round-trips (structure, reactive deltas, action
103: and value dispatch) in `tests/roundtrip.rs`.

## Testing

```sh
cd pathland-waterui && cargo test
```

Runs the producer round-trips in `tests/roundtrip.rs`: structure, reactive
deltas, action and value dispatch, and the lossless round trip (emit → decode →
rebuild → re-emit).

The round-trip tests need a decoder that applies frames to a retained tree and
rebuilds WaterUI views from it — `tests/support/consumer.rs` (`TestConsumer`).
It is **test support only**, not part of the runtime API. Unlike the demo,
which uses the real `pathland-render-html` renderer's retained node tree, the
test decoder keeps a declarative description (component, text, properties,
children) with no native elements.

**Why a retained decoder?** The protocol is delta-based: each delta frame
references existing nodes by id and carries only the change, so a decoder must
keep the tree it has built so far — exactly as a rendering backend keeps its
output tree (e.g. the DOM). `TestConsumer` is that retained output tree in
miniature, kept so the tests can assert on accumulated state and prove a full
WaterUI round trip is lossless.

Yes — the demo already depends on the `waterui` umbrella (added for the border), but it still imports the individual `waterui_core`/`waterui_layout`/`waterui_text`/`waterui_controls` crates directly. Those are all re-exported through the umbrella, so the imports can collapse.

## Proposed change

Replace lines 26–34 (9 lines across 4 crates + `waterui::color::*` + `ViewExt`) with umbrella-only imports:

```rust
use waterui::color::{Color, signal_color};
use waterui::component::{button, hstack, slider, toggle, vstack};
use waterui::component::text::text; // the function only (module shares the name)
use waterui::reactive::binding;
use waterui::{Binding, Computed, Environment, SignalExt, View, ViewExt};
```

(5 lines, all from `waterui`; drops the 4 direct crate imports.)

## Why not `waterui::prelude::*`

`prelude::*` would pull in `waterui_core`'s `State`, which **collides** with `axum::extract::State` that the demo uses for handlers. Importing specific names avoids touching the handler code. (Verified from the codebase: `waterui::component` re-exports `waterui_controls::*` plus `hstack`/`vstack` and the `text` function; `Binding`/`Computed`/`Environment`/`SignalExt`/`View`/`ViewExt` are all at the `waterui::` root; `binding` is at `waterui::reactive::binding`.)

## Verification

- `cargo build` the demo (needs the Xcode env vars) — confirms every import resolves and no unused-import warnings appear.
- If any "unused import" warning shows for a name that is both a module and a function (e.g. `slider`), fall back to the gallery's explicit sub-path form (`use waterui::component::slider::slider;`).

## Optional follow-up

After the import change, `waterui-core`, `waterui-layout`, `waterui-text`, `waterui-controls` in the demo's `Cargo.toml` are no longer referenced directly (only transitively via `waterui`), so they can be removed too.
